United States Section, International Boundary and Water Commission, United States and Mexico (USIBWC).ACTION: Notice of availability.
The USIBWC hereby gives notice that the Draft Environmental Assessment (EA) and Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) for the Reconstruction of the Fort Hancock-El Porvenir International Bridge, Rio Grande Rectification Project, Hudspeth County, Texas is available.
Elizabeth Verdecchia, Natural Resources Specialist, Telephone: (915) 832-4701, email: elizabeth.verdecchia@ibwc.gov.
The electronic version of the Draft EA and FONSI is available at the USIBWC web page: https://www.ibwc.gov/​reports-studies/​eis-ea-public-comment/​. Public comments may be submitted to Elizabeth Verdecchia, Natural Resources Specialist, USIBWC, 4191 N Mesa, El Paso, Texas 79902; email: elizabeth.verdecchia@ibwc.gov.
The USIBWC is proposing to construct a new bridge section on the U.S. side of the Fort Hancock—El Porvenir International Bridge that would tie-in to the Mexican section of the bridge, in order to address structural and safety issues with the bridge. Pursuant to Section 102(2)(c) of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) of 1969, as amended, and the USIBWC Operational Procedures for Implementing Section 102 of NEPA, published in the Federal Register September 2, 1981, USIBWC developed a Draft EA that analyzed the Action Alternative (Preferred Alternative) and the No Action Alternative. The Action Alternative—U.S. Side Rebuild to Same Profile would construct a new bridge section on the U.S. side to address with the structural integrity of the substructure and bridge deck. The new bridge section on the U.S. side would tie-in to the Mexican section of the bridge, which is in good condition. The new bridge section would generally match the existing bridge with regard to having the same height and width, similar roadway and sidewalk, but with an improved floodgate. Under the No Action Alternative, USIBWC would not construct a new bridge section, and the safety issues would not be addressed.
Potential impacts on natural, cultural, and other resources were evaluated. A Finding of No Significant Impact for the Proposed Action, based on a review of the facts and analyses contained in the EA. An environmental impact statement will not be prepared.
USIBWC Deputy Chief Counsel, International Boundary and Water Commission, United States Section.

title: Nvidia spy scandal exposes Singapore’s role in China’s AI chip trade
zh_title: 英伟达间谍丑闻暴露了新加坡在中国人工智能芯片贸易中的作用
summary: 一家鲜为人知的新加坡公司与一名据称与英伟达的黄仁勋有染的中国间谍有联系，这暴露了新加坡在美国先进人工智能处理器对华贸易中日益重要的地位。 Megaspeed 的股东曾包括美国芯片制造商首席执行官爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang)，她是英伟达最大的亚洲客户之一，其资产负债表从 2023 年的 3300 万美元飙升至一年后的 30 亿美元。该公司的突然崛起是通过成为 [Nvidia](https://www.ft.com/nvidia) 和 Megaspeed 的 b 之间的渠道而实现的。
content:
一家鲜为人知的新加坡公司与一名据称与英伟达的黄仁勋有染的中国间谍有联系，这暴露了新加坡在美国先进人工智能处理器对华贸易中日益重要的地位。

Megaspeed 的股东曾包括美国芯片制造商首席执行官爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang)，她是英伟达最大的亚洲客户之一，其资产负债表从 2023 年的 3300 万美元飙升至一年后的 30 亿美元。

该公司的突然崛起是通过成为 [Nvidia](https://www.ft.com/nvidia) 和 Megaspeed 最大客户中国科技集团阿里巴巴之间的渠道而实现的。

虽然新加坡不一定禁止向中国公司转让先进的人工智能芯片，但此类交易可能违反美国的出口管制。这个城市国家面临着来自华盛顿越来越大的压力，要求打击涉嫌为此类转移提供便利的公司。

Nvidia 的处理器已成为人工智能基础设施的关键© David Paul Morris/Bloomberg

美国当局一直在调查 Megaspeed 涉嫌违反美国芯片出口限制的行为，而新加坡警方也在对该公司展开调查。

Megaspeed表示，它已成为美国和马来西亚当局调查的对象，但“没有证据表明存在任何涉及非法转让芯片或任何非法活动的违规行为”。
但这起案件暴露了通过新加坡运营的中介网络，帮助中国科技公司获得先进的美国芯片，同时引发了人们对这个城市国家在华盛顿限制中国获取人工智能技术的努力中所扮演的角色的质疑。

该城邦是 Nvidia 在 2025 财年的全球第二大计费中心(https://www.ft.com/content/6b1ce190-24d4-4f39-a518-ef9dae5fa2c4)，占总收入的 18%。然而，只有 2% 的收入来自实际进入该国的芯片。许多亚洲公司通过新加坡办事处下芯片订单，但产品直接发送给他们。

新加坡人工智能公司顾问马蒂亚斯·亨德里克斯(Matthias Hendrichs)表示：“新加坡拥有独特的地位，因为它与美国和中国都有非常牢固的经济联系，这意味着当不可能进行更直接的接触时，它往往是两国之间的渠道。”“它在灰色市场中的作用是新加坡与两个超级大国关系密切的结果，也是它必须管理的事情。”

Megaspeed 表示，它已成为美国和马来西亚当局调查的对象© Taryn Ng/AFP/Getty Images

Megaspeed 成立于 2015 年，是一家中国视频游戏开发商的新加坡子公司。 2023年3月，它被英属维尔京群岛一家名为Huang Le Ltd.的公司收购。
虽然该公司的所有权并未公开披露，但黄乐的中文名字是 Alice Huang，她被列为 Megaspeed 的董事总经理。

Alice Huang 向中国投资者推销了她与阿里巴巴的商业关系，并吹捧她有能力获得 Nvidia 珍贵的图形处理单元，英国《金融时报》[本周报道](https://www.ft.com/content/5d8c1e1d-6ce0-4eb4-9f5c-722fa5c4841d)。她经常被拍到与黄仁勋一起出席行业活动。美国当局怀疑她被中国情报部门招募。

2023 年 11 月，Megaspeed 再次出售给一家名为 Swiftdata 的新加坡实体。陈永邦,

【原文 English Original】
A little-known Singaporean company linked to an alleged Chinese spy believed to have had an affair with Nvidia’s Jensen Huang has exposed the city-state’s growing importance in the trade in advanced US AI processors to China.

Megaspeed — whose shareholders once included Alice Huang, the businesswoman at the centre of scandal engulfing the US chipmaker’s chief — became one of Nvidia’s biggest Asian customers, with its balance sheet surging from $33mn in 2023 to $3bn a year later.

The company’s sudden rise came through being a conduit between [Nvidia](https://www.ft.com/nvidia) and Megaspeed’s biggest customer, the Chinese tech group Alibaba.

While Singapore does not necessarily prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to Chinese companies, such transactions can breach US export controls. The city-state has come under growing pressure from Washington to crack down on companies suspected of facilitating such transfers.

Nvidia’s processors have become crucial to AI infrastructure© David Paul Morris/Bloomberg

US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed over suspected violations of US chip export restrictions, while Singaporean police are conducting their own probe into the company.

Megaspeed has said it has been the subject of investigations by US and Malaysian authorities, but there has been “no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities”.

But the case has exposed the network of intermediaries that operate through [Singapore](https://www.ft.com/singapore), helping Chinese tech companies gain access to advanced US chips while raising questions about the city-state’s role in Washington’s efforts to restrict China’s access to AI technology.

The city-state was Nvidia’s [second-biggest billing centre](https://www.ft.com/content/6b1ce190-24d4-4f39-a518-ef9dae5fa2c4) globally in the 2025 fiscal year, accounting for 18 per cent of total revenue. Yet only 2 per cent of revenue was for chips that actually entered the country. Many Asian companies place chip orders through their Singapore office, but the products are sent to them directly.

“Singapore has a unique position because it has very strong economic ties to both the US and China, which means it is often the conduit between the two when more direct access is not possible,” said Matthias Hendrichs, a Singapore-based adviser to AI companies.“Its role in grey markets is a consequence of Singapore’s close ties to both superpowers and is something it has to manage.”

Megaspeed says it has been the subject of investigations by US and Malaysian authorities© Taryn Ng/AFP/Getty Images

Megaspeed began life in 2015 as the Singaporean subsidiary of a Chinese video game developer. In March 2023, it was bought by a British Virgin Islands company called Huang Le Ltd.

While the ownership of that business is not publicly disclosed, Huang Le is the Chinese name of Alice Huang, and she was listed as the managing director of Megaspeed.

Alice Huang had pitched her commercial relationship with Alibaba to China-based investors and touted her ability to secure Nvidia’s prized graphics processing units, the FT [reported this week](https://www.ft.com/content/5d8c1e1d-6ce0-4eb4-9f5c-722fa5c4841d). She has been regularly pictured with Jensen Huang at industry events. US authorities have come to suspect she was recruited by Chinese intelligence services.

In November 2023, Megaspeed was sold again to a Singaporean entity called Swiftdata. Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, a Singaporean with close business links to China according to company filings, is listed as the sole director of both Swiftdata and Megaspeed.

Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan© LinkedIn

Company filings also show that Alibaba, through a Singaporean subsidiary called Apex Enterprise Solutions, lent money to Megaspeed, through its Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix, in June 2024. As part of the agreement, Speedmatrix pledged its entire business as collateral for the loan.

FT reporting has shown Megaspeed leaned on its relationship with Alibaba to become designated by Nvidia as an official “cloud partner”, which authorised the business to buy GPUs from the US chipmaker in order to sell computing services via mostly leased facilities across south-east Asia.

The Chinese tech giant was Megaspeed’s anchor customer for its south-east Asian cloud service operation and became its largest client, the FT also reported.

Towards the end of last year, US authorities began investigating Megaspeed over suspicions that it helped divert Nvidia chips to China. Singapore police also began a probe into the business, and data centre companies started terminating their contracts with the company. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing.

“Trying to control the use of GPUs is a game of whack-a-mole,” said Paul Mah, senior adviser specialising in data centres in south-east Asia at consultancy Flint Global. “It’s not just hard to police chip movements, it’s impossible.”

Nvidia’s top-tier Blackwell chip, which is restricted from sale to China by the US© SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg

Attention has grown on Singapore-based companies — often with Chinese executives or people with close business links to China — using Malaysian subsidiaries or close trading partners to transfer Nvidia chips.

Malaysia has become a major Asian hub for data centres that provide computing power to Chinese companies.

In a different case, police [raided 22 locations](https://www.ft.com/content/d940249a-29a8-4d0e-b324-a5e65c1ed1a9?syn-25a6b1a6=1) in February 2025 across the city-state and arrested nine people in a case involving the sale of Dell, Supermicro and Asus servers — which were suspected of containing Nvidia chips — that were imported from the US and then sold to a company in Malaysia.

Three Singaporeans and a Chinese national were charged with fraud in the case, as well as the companies involved. Officials said the scheme relied on paperwork that gave a false impression of the ultimate destination of the servers.

It involved a Singaporean computer equipment sales company called Luxuriate Your Life and another local business, Aperia Cloud Services, which described itself on its website as being Nvidia’s first qualified cloud partner in south-east Asia and “uniquely positioned with priority access to the highest performing GPUs available in the market”.

A S$55mn ($43mn) luxury property near Singapore’s Botanic Gardens belonging to Aperia chief executive Wei Zhaolun, also known as Alan Wei, was seized by police in June. He was later charged with money laundering. Wei has pleaded not guilty to the charges. Aperia has denied the allegations against the business.

The high-profile cases have shone a spotlight on the networks that facilitate the flow of US chips across Asia. But Mah said their exposure may also lead to these trade routes being disrupted.

“The additional scrutiny in Singapore will probably lead shipments to take place in other countries where there is less oversight,” he said. “Then it will be much harder to track.”

Nvidia, Megaspeed, Alibaba, Aperia, Luxuriate Your Life and lawyers for Wei did not respond to requests for comment. Calls to Alice Huang went unanswered.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Monday the spy allegation was groundless, describing it as a smear and defamation.

_Additional reporting by Zijing Wu in Hong Kong_

title: Acquitted 'China spy' Chris Cash: I was fall guy for security services but also naive
zh_title: “中国间谍”克里斯·卡什被无罪释放：我是安全部门的替罪羊，但也很天真
summary: 17小时前网站搜索政治调查记者乔·派克和政治记者菲尔·坎普一名被指控为中国从事间谍活动的英国男子告诉BBC，他是英国警察和安全部门的“方便替罪羊”，他们希望将外国的间谍威胁“放在地图上”。前议会研究员克里斯·卡什 (Chris Cash) 与我们分享了 6,000 多条信息，揭露了一名中国官员如何寻求有关英国敏感政治事务的信息，其中包括 2022 年保守党领导层之争，以决定下一任首相。这些消息显示了现金如何
content:
站内搜索

17 小时前

乔·派克（Joe Pike），政治调查记者

菲尔·坎普，政治记者

一名被指控为中国从事间谍活动的英国男子告诉英国广播公司，他是英国警察和安全部门“方便的替罪羊”，他们希望将外国的间谍威胁“放在地图上”。

前议会研究员克里斯·卡什 (Chris Cash) 与我们分享了 6,000 多条信息，揭露了一名中国官员如何寻求有关英国敏感政治事务的信息，其中包括 2022 年保守党领导层之争，以决定下一任首相。

这些信息显示了卡什在中国的朋友克里斯·贝里（他一直与他分享信息）如何戏剧性地描述了贝里与一名中国高级官员之间的“秘密”会面。

贝里表示，他被告知中国担心其制裁的一名英国议员可能会如何晋升到内阁职位。

这些信息还透露了卡什在议会通行证审查过程中如何使用他的朋友作为推荐人，该通行证已获得批准。

与卡什一样，贝瑞也被指控从事间谍活动。两人始终坚称自己无罪。

卡什无罪释放引发了一场关于政府未能将中国列为“威胁”的政治争论，卡什在被无罪释放后的首次采访中表示，他“永远不会做任何损害英国国家安全的事情”。
但他承认，自己向朋友发送“八卦”短信是“不专业和天真的”。他是在 2018 年认识的，当时他们都在中国的一所学校教英语。

尽管大量信息显示他正在讨论敏感话题，但没有证据表明卡什是由中国共产党支付或同情中国共产党的。

克里斯·卡什（左）和克里斯·贝里于 2018 年在中国教书时相识

由于政府此前曾表示，中国间谍正在以日益复杂的间谍活动瞄准英国政治、国防和商业部门的官员，卡什认为，追查他的案件是为了向其他人发出警告。

贝里拒绝对此事发表评论，但在无罪释放时表示，他否认有任何不当行为，并且“受到媒体不公平的审判”。

他表示，他已向一家中国公司提供了报告，他相信该公司的客户寻求与英国建立贸易联系，这些报告不包含机密信息，并且依赖于公共来源。

卡什于 2019 年返回英国，他在中国工作的辞职信中表示，他感到“袖手旁观并参与一个令我感到不舒服的体系”。

后来，他成为威斯敏斯特对中国持怀疑态度的保守党议员管理的一个小型政策小组的主任。

与此同时，贝瑞留在中国为一家大型咨询公司撰写报告，该咨询公司与许多中国公司一样，与政府有联系。
* 观看：[BBC 新闻 YouTube 频道的中国间谍案内幕](https://youtu.be/jGKBA6xaflE)

英国安全部门声称，这些男子在 2022 年 1 月至 2023 年 3 月期间通过加密消息应用程序 Signal 发送的消息中的信息已被传递给与中国政府有关的人。

英格兰和威尔士的最高检察官表示，此案去年秋天已经失败，因为政府官员当时不能说中国被列为“敌人”。

这引发了英国为安抚中国政府而进行政治干预的指控。

中国此前称有关间谍活动的指控“纯属捏造和恶意诽谤”。

A British man who was charged with spying for China has told the BBC he was a "convenient fall guy" for UK police and security services who wanted to put espionage threats by foreign states "on the map".

Chris Cash, a former parliamentary researcher, has shared more than 6,000 messages with us revealing how a Chinese official sought information about sensitive political matters in the UK - including the 2022 Tory leadership battle to decide the next prime minister.

The messages show how Cash's friend in China, Chris Berry - with whom he had been sharing information - dramatically described a "secret" meeting between Berry and a high-ranking Chinese official.

Berry said he had been told that China was concerned about how a British MP it had sanctioned might be promoted to a cabinet role.

The messages also reveal how Cash used his friend as a reference during vetting for a parliamentary pass - which was approved.

Like Cash, Berry was also charged with espionage. The two men consistently maintained their innocence.

In Cash's first interview since his acquittal, which sparked a political row over the government's failure to designate China as a "threat", he says he would "never do anything" to harm UK national security.

But he admits he was "unprofessional and naive" to send "gossiping" texts to his friend, whom he met in 2018 when they both taught English in a school in China.

Although the trove of messages shows him discussing sensitive topics, there is no evidence in them that Cash was paid by, or sympathetic to, the Chinese Communist Party.

Chris Cash, left, and Chris Berry met in 2018 when they were teaching in China

With the government having previously said that Chinese spies were targeting UK officials across the political, defence and business sectors with increasingly sophisticated espionage operations, Cash believes his case was pursued as a warning to others.

Berry declined to comment on this story, but at the time of his acquittal said he denied any wrongdoing and that he had been "unfairly subjected to a trial by media".

He said he had provided reports to a Chinese company, which he believed had clients seeking to develop trading links with the UK, and those reports contained no classified information and relied on public sources.

Cash returned to the UK in 2019, saying in his resignation message for his job in China that he felt "guilty sitting back and participating in a system that I am uncomfortable with".

He later became the director of a small policy group run by China-sceptic Conservative MPs in Westminster.

Meanwhile, Berry stayed in China writing reports for a large consultancy which, like many Chinese companies, has links to the government.

*   Watch: [Inside the China Spy Case on the BBC News YouTube channel](https://youtu.be/jGKBA6xaflE)

UK security services alleged that information from the men's messages, sent on the encrypted messaging app Signal between January 2022 and March 2023, had been passed to people linked to the Chinese state.

England and Wales' top prosecutor said the case had collapsed last autumn because government officials could not say China had been classed as an "enemy" at the time.

This prompted accusations of UK political interference to placate the Chinese government.

China has previously called the allegations of spying "pure fabrication and malicious slander".

## 'A psychological game of chess'

The most striking section of the messages handed to the BBC concerns Berry's account of his meeting in summer 2022 with a senior Chinese official who wanted to have "a more detailed co-operation".

In voice notes Berry describes how, beforehand, work colleagues had told him the official's interest had been piqued by reports Berry had written, which included details of the UK's foreign policy approach to China.

In the voice notes, Berry says he was initially aghast, but then decided: "I thought it would be interesting to go anyway… not really intending to do anything."

Berry tells Cash he was driven to a government-owned villa in a grand compound.

The experience "felt like a psychological game of chess" and "like a test", Berry says.

He kept his hands under the table as tea was served: "I didn't want it to be obvious if I was nervous. I tested to see if my hands were shaking first, then drank the tea."

Berry describes the senior Chinese official asking via an interpreter "about the situation in the UK at the moment, about the Tory leadership thing".

At that time, Boris Johnson had just resigned as the UK's prime minister, and a Conservative leadership battle was taking place, which Liz Truss would go on to win.

Berry says he jokingly tried to ask his host which candidate China wanted, but the interpreter did not translate his question.

"And then the main guy just shakes my hand like it's time to go," Berry tells Cash.

After receiving the voice notes, Cash replies via text the next day: "You, my friend, have just been elite captured" before adding: "You're in spy territory now".

In many media reports these particular messages, previously released in a government witness statement, have been presented as a smoking gun - evidence that Cash knew his friend was passing on information to the Chinese state.

But Cash insists it was a "tongue-in-cheek joke" because he knew his friend to be "a staunch critic of the Chinese Communist Party".

The next morning, he made a joke about Berry spying for the UK and getting in trouble with the Chinese authorities, he says. Cash texted: "Keep him sweet… We may have a use for you yet".

"I didn't believe he was knowingly spying on the UK through me," says Cash. "I trusted my friend… I wish I had seen the danger earlier, spotted it and cut off all contact."

## 'Bigger deal than I thought'

So who was the mystery official Berry had met?

"I found out who this guy is," Berry text-messaged Cash a few hours later. "Bigger deal than I thought."

Berry posted a link to the Wikipedia page of Cai Qi, who at the time was one of China's most influential politicians and is now, in effect, President Xi Jinping's chief of staff.

Berry identified Cai Qi (left) as the man he had met - a trusted aide of Chinese President Xi Jinping

Whether Berry correctly identified his host remains unclear. He has since disputed the suggestion that he met someone as senior as Cai Qi.

What is beyond dispute is that he believed he may have met someone highly placed within the Chinese political system.

For Chris Cash, this unusual encounter did not prompt alarm bells. Asked why not, Cash tells the BBC: "Because I didn't think anything of the meeting, really."

We ask Cash why his friend might have been asked to such a meeting. "Strange things happen in China... you know we would often brush shoulders with sort of quite senior members of the Chinese communist party," he tells us.

Challenged about whether he had read the Wikipedia link at the time, Cash says he had "skimmed it", adding that it described him as a judge and a provincial-level official. "I just thought it was a weird meeting with a guy who'd taken an interest," he says.

Six months later, Berry said in text messages that "off the record" he had it "on pretty good authority" that China was considering dropping sanctions against Tom Tugendhat, one of the Conservative MPs in the China Research Group, where Cash worked.

Berry wrote that this would happen as long as the West "continued to show signals that they are willing to work together".

The Chinese believed it would be "extremely embarrassing" if Tugendhat became prime minister or foreign secretary while under Chinese sanctions, Berry said.

At the time of the meeting in summer 2022, China-sceptic Tugendhat was seen as a possible contender to succeed Boris Johnson, or become UK foreign secretary.

He was actually appointed as security minister by Liz Truss, and Beijing lifted sanctions on him in January 2026.

Was Cash concerned that Berry appeared to be passing information to him about Chinese foreign policy?

Cash says he assumed Berry had heard this "through the grapevine at his company" which was doing business with the UK.

He says he never doubted his friend's trustworthiness, to the extent he even named Berry as a reference on his application for a security pass for the Palace of Westminster.

The pass was granted and, a fortnight before their arrests in early 2023, Cash invited Berry to Parliament for lunch.

It was to be their final face-to-face conversation.

## 'Complete shock'

Cash was in bed at quarter to six on a March morning when he was woken by car doors being shut, he says. Within seconds, four UK counter-terrorism officers had barged into his bedroom at his parents' home in Edinburgh.

"They told me to sit up and not touch anything and then said I was under arrest for breaching the Official Secrets Act," Cash says.

"I was in complete shock… quivering... My mum was hysterical."

Cash says the officers dressed him in dirty clothes he had worn that weekend, handcuffed him and marched him down to an unmarked police car. He was later driven to London.

Chris Berry was also arrested the same day.

It remains unclear how, when and why British security services became interested in the exchanges between the two friends.

But they are likely to have found out far more about their relationship when Berry was stopped and questioned by counter-terror officers at Heathrow Airport.

His laptop and phone were taken - this may have enabled his Signal chats to be downloaded.

Berry later messaged Cash about it.

Cash says he had not been alarmed by this: "I thought it was just standard... for a guy who'd been in China."

As the investigation progressed, it became clear the authorities believed Cash and Berry had been involved in an informal, but dangerous, exchange of information that was "prejudicial to the safety and interests of the UK".

The allegations were based on 6,273 messages between the pair - the same ones Cash has now shared with the BBC. Cash's solicitor has told the BBC they are genuine.

They cover a period when Cash had joined the China Research Group (CRG), founded by Tugendhat and fellow Tory MP Alicia Kearns, and when Berry was working for a Chinese company called Strong, where part of his work involved writing political and economic reports for clients.

According to court documents, Berry was said to have compiled 34 reports for a man linked to the Chinese state spy agency, relaying information passed on to him by Cash. Strong did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

The CRG's office was across the Thames from Westminster, but Cash regularly had meetings in Parliament. Cash did not have government security clearance and there is no evidence he had access to classified documents.

Despite being thousands of miles apart, the two friends remained in close contact, often messaging daily.

The messages reviewed by the BBC show them discussing topics including sanctions on China, the tech company Huawei, human rights, Hong Kong, Taiwan and British foreign policy.

Cash says he used the Signal app for almost all his contacts with people in China - "more for their protection" - as he says discussing the government "could land someone… in trouble". He and Berry did not use the app's "disappearing messages" function.

Much of the information they discussed was publicly available, says Cash - who has given the BBC a detailed spreadsheet with links and references in an attempt to prove it.

# 因间谍罪被无罪释放的前议会助手告诉 BBC，他是“替罪羊”，但也“天真”

一名因为中国从事间谍活动而被判无罪的英国男子告诉英国广播公司，对于英国警察和安全部门来说，他是一个“方便的替罪羊”，他们希望将外国的间谍威胁“放在地图上”。

前议会研究员克里斯·卡什 (Chris Cash) 与我们分享了 6000 多条信息，揭示了一名中国官员如何寻求有关英国敏感政治事务的信息，其中包括 2022 年保守党领导层之争，以决定下一任首相。

卡什无罪释放后首次接受采访时承认，他向当时在中国的朋友克里斯·贝里发送“八卦”短信是“不专业和天真的”。无罪释放引发了一场关于政府未能将中国列为“威胁”的政治争论。

贝里也被判无罪释放间谍罪，他拒绝对此事发表评论，但此前否认有任何不当行为，并表示自己“受到了媒体的不公平审判”。

BBC 政治调查记者乔·派克 (Joe Pike) 向卡什讲述了这些指控。

title: Jensen Huang: What we know about Nvidia CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy
zh_title: 黄仁勋：我们对英伟达首席执行官与涉嫌中国间谍的恋情了解多少
summary: 15 小时前 北美科技记者 Lily Jamali 和商业记者 Peter Hoskins 人工智能 (AI) 行业最重要的人物之一被指控与一名疑似中国间谍有染。据《纽约时报》报道，美国情报官员认为，与英伟达首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋关系密切的中国女商人爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）是北京的间谍。黄仁勋 [承认](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/a-message-to-our-company)
content:
15 小时前

Lily Jamali，北美科技记者

彼得·霍斯金斯，商业记者

人工智能（AI）行业最重要的人物之一被指控与一名疑似中国间谍有染。

据《纽约时报》报道，美国情报官员认为，与英伟达首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋关系密切的中国女商人爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）是北京的间谍。

黄仁勋[承认](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/a-message-to-our-company)对妻子“不忠”，并为伤害她和孩子而道歉。

全球最有价值的公司之一英伟达已对此事展开独立调查。

该公司表示，不认为美国国家安全受到损害，并补充说黄仁勋致力于继续领导该公司。

以下是我们对这起事件的了解以及它的重要性。

## 黄爱丽丝是谁？

黄仁勋（左）和 Alice Huang（又名黄乐）在活动中

[《纽约时报》报道](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/technology/nvidia-investigation-jensen-huang-china.html)，美国官员认为 Alice Huang 已被中国最高情报机构招募从事间谍活动。她目前下落不明。
Alice Huang 与 Jensen Huang 没有关系，她在 2023 年 3 月至 11 月期间担任新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高管。

该公司曾被怀疑帮助将英伟达芯片转移到中国。英伟达表示，此事已被调查并被揭穿。

然而，Megaspeed 正在接受新加坡政府的调查，原因是此前有指控称该公司规避美国对 Nvidia 高端芯片出口的制裁。

BBC 已联系 Megaspeed 征求意见。

据报道，监控显示了爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）与一名美国公民之间的通信，该公民随后被确认为黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）。

目前尚不清楚黄乐（又名黄乐）据称收集并传递给北京的情报（如果有的话）。

当 BBC 询问英伟达是否意识到情报问题时，该公司表示没有。

英伟达发言人告诉 BBC：“我们相信，如果我们成为真正威胁的目标，美国政府就会通知我们。”

中国否认了间谍指控。

外交部发言人郭家琨表示：“有关中国间谍的指控完全毫无根据，纯属猜测，意在抹黑、攻击中国。”

十月份有媒体报道称，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普去年曾听取过有关指控黄爱丽代表中国进行间谍活动的情报简报。
当被问及是否希望自己“根据情报采取行动”时，特朗普告诉记者：“不，我不这么认为。我认为他（黄仁勋）是一个值得尊敬的人。”

与此同时，美国国务卿马可·卢比奥在被问及黄仁勋时拒绝发表评论。

据报道，今年春天，国务卿监督起草了一份备忘录，警告特朗普政府有关黄仁勋与这位中国女商人的关系。

## 为什么这很重要？

英伟达是[美国和中国人工智能竞赛的核心](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6gqdgg8w59xo)，这就是为什么这位亿万富翁老板的事件引发了美国立法者对国家安全的担忧。

特朗普曾说过“谁赢得了人工智能的胜利”，而骗局

【原文 English Original】
15 hours ago

Lily Jamali,North America Technology correspondent and

Peter Hoskins,Business reporter

One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang, [was a spy for Beijing](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3dxw10rjn9no), according to a New York Times report.

Jensen Huang [admitted](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/a-message-to-our-company) to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.

Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair.

It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang is committed to continuing to lead the company.

Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters.

## Who is Alice Huang?

Jensen Huang (left) and Alice Huang - also known as Huang Le - at an event

US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, [the New York Times reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/technology/nvidia-investigation-jensen-huang-china.html). Her current whereabouts are unknown.

Alice Huang, no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023.

The company had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia said this was investigated and debunked.

However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips.

The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment.

Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang.

It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing.

When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not.

"We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC.

China has rejected the spying allegations.

Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said: "The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China."

There were media reports in October that US President Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf.

On whether he wished he had "acted on the intelligence", Trump told journalists: "No, I don't think so. I think he's [Jensen Huang] an honourable guy."

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Jensen Huang.

In spring this year, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Jensen Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman.

## Why does it matter?

Nvidia is [at the heart of US and China's AI race](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6gqdgg8w59xo), which is why the billionaire boss's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers.

Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the concern is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities.

The US advantage is in large part because of companies like Nvidia, working with producers such as the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips.

Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security.

This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero.

Jensen Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way.

The revelations may explain why Jensen Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to [sell all but its most advanced chips to China](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqxz29pe1v0o).

## Who is Jensen Huang?

Nvidia boss Jensen Huang and US President Donald Trump at the White House

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

He worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and [once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech"](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq55ek28z98o), he has a reputation as a workaholic with incredibly high standards for his staff.

He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Jensen Huang.

Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang after reports emerged about Alice Huang and her alledged links to the Chinese state and asked him: "'Did you have any idea she was a spy?

"He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," said Trump.

## What investigations are now under way?

Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into the affair and has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

It will be led by Joon Kim, a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District who is now at litigation partner at the law firm.

US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was also [investigating the affair](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqg7x7dpvym8o). The FBI declined to comment further when contacted by the BBC.

Jensen Huang has also been asked to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees on 18 November.

Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee asked the Nvidia chief executive to appear to explain his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage.

Jensen Huang has yet to say he will comply, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC.

## What is Nvidia and how important is it?

There is no clear successor for Jensen Huang at Nvidia

Founded by Jensen Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games.

Eventually it [changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crmp9mppvzro).

Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch.

Huang bet on AI at a time when "there were no customers for the stuff he was building", Witt told the BBC.

Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure like Amazon, Google and Microsoft now use Nvidia chips.

Currently worth about $4tn, Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world.

For now, the firm's board appears unlikely to remove Jensen Huang, saying on Sunday they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team".

Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake.

There is no public succession plan for the 63-year-old. He has often said he hopes to continue in the role for decades, and Bloomberg reports he has created an informal leadership structure around him unlike a traditional company's hierarchy.

His children, Spencer and Madison, and son-in-law Nico Caprez work at Nvidia in senior roles.

## Who is Jensen Huang's wife?

Lori Huang and her husband at a state dinner by Trump for his Chinese President Xi Jinping

Jensen Huang met his future wife Lori Mills at Oregon State University while studying electrical engineering in the early 1980s. The pair were lab partners.

They married in 1985 and have two children, Madison and Spencer.

In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation. The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn.

Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University.

Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, adding: "That's very important to him".

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."

_Additional reporting by Tom McArthur in London, Ayeshea Perera and Tessa Wong in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney_

content:
西班牙足球运动员去世后，前精工足球俱乐部门将敦促国际足联审查球员安全中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 12 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
西班牙足球运动员去世后，前精工足球俱乐部门将敦促国际足联审查球员安全
西班牙足球运动员赫苏斯·德·米格尔在比赛中因碰撞死亡后，马来西亚和香港精工足球俱乐部的前门将林凤记呼吁国际足联审查球员安全协议。
西班牙足球运动员赫苏斯·德米格尔最近在一场比赛中死亡后，前马来西亚门将林凤记敦促国际足联重新审查球员安全协议。
据马来西亚在线新闻刊物 Weekly-Echo 报道，这位 74 岁的老人曾在 1970 年代担任马来西亚队和香港精工队的守门员，他将这一事件描述为“一场悲惨的生命损失”。 25岁的米格尔是西班牙乙级联赛特内里费队的前锋，11月3日在前一天的一场比赛中与安道尔足球俱乐部门将赫苏斯·奥沃诺相撞后死亡。
“我自己也当过守门员，所以我会研究事件的机制。这是一个瞬间的误判，导致了一场灾难，”林指出。 “奥沃诺的意图不可避免地会受到审视。他抬起膝盖是为了保护自己、增高还是造成伤害？”林解释说，守门员如此高速的干预使得碰撞几乎不可避免。他提出了奥沃诺的行为是否鲁莽或仅仅是本能反应的问题。
他还对奥沃诺表示担忧，奥沃诺在事件中幸存下来，但现在可能面临压倒性的内疚和心理创伤。 “他也需要心理帮助，”林说。他指出，现在守门员经常被要求离开禁区，这增加了与对方球员发生危险碰撞的可能性。
林说：“一名球员已经死亡，不要再杀死另一名球员。”他呼吁国际足联审查球员安全措施，以确保这样的悲剧不再发生。他还敦促国际足联不仅要考虑人身安全，还要考虑场上悲剧的心理影响，并为所有受影响的各方提供支持。
他讲述了自己在球场上受伤的经历，包括 1971 年鼻子骨折和 1975 年手腕骨折，以强调球员面临的危险。林指出，奥沃诺和其他相关人员可能会遭受内疚、震惊、焦虑、抑郁和其他心理影响，可能包括噩梦或害怕重返比赛。他补充说，目击者也可能因目睹此类事件而遭受情感创伤。
负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

Thursday, 12 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Former Seiko FC goalkeeper urges FIFA to review player safety after Spanish footballer's death
Lim Fung Kee, former goalkeeper for Malaysia and Hong Kong's Seiko FC, calls on FIFA to review player safety protocols after Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel died following a collision during a match.
Former Malaysian goalkeeper Lim Fung Kee has urged FIFA to reexamine player safety protocols in the wake of the recent death of Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel during a match.
According to Malaysian online news publication Weekly-Echo, the 74-year-old, who played as a goalkeeper for Malaysia in the 1970s and for Hong Kong's Seiko FC, described the incident as "a tragic loss of life." Miguel, 25, a striker for CD Tenerife in Spain's Second Division, died on 3 November after a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a match a day before.
"Having been a goalkeeper myself, I look at the mechanics of the incident. It was a split-second miscalculation that resulted in a catastrophe," Lim noted. "Owono's intention will inevitably come under scrutiny. Did he raise his knees to protect himself, gain height or inflict injury?" Lim explained that such high-speed interventions by goalkeepers can make collisions almost inevitable. He raised the question of whether Owono's actions were reckless or simply an instinctive reaction.
He also expressed concern for Owono, who survived the incident but may now face overwhelming guilt and psychological trauma. "He needs psychological help too," Lim said. He noted that goalkeepers are now often required to leave their penalty areas, increasing the likelihood of dangerous collisions with opposing players.
"One player has died, don't kill another," Lim said, calling on FIFA to review player safety measures to ensure that such a tragedy does not happen again. He also urged FIFA to consider not only physical safety, but also the psychological impact of on-field tragedies, and to provide support for all affected parties.
He recounted his own injuries on the pitch, including a broken nose in 1971 and a fractured wrist in 1975, to highlight the dangers faced by players. Lim noted that Owono and others involved could suffer from guilt, shock, anxiety, depression, and other psychological effects, possibly including nightmares or fear of returning to play. He added that witnesses may also experience emotional trauma from witnessing such an event.

香港珠宝代表团访问新加坡，宣传贸易枢纽的作用和增长|中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 12 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港珠宝代表团访问新加坡宣传贸易枢纽作用和增长
香港驻新加坡贸易办事处与通过贸易通平台来访的珠宝代表团共同举办了商务午餐。官员们强调了创纪录的出口增长、该市作为贸易中心的作用，以及到 2027 年第一季度建立黄金清算系统的计划。
香港驻新加坡经济贸易办事处于 11 月 11 日与通过政府“贸易通”平台访问新加坡的珠宝业代表团共同举办商务联谊午餐会。此次午餐会汇聚了约80位来自香港和新加坡的商界领袖、行业代表和买家。
办事处主任洪宝莉在致辞中强调香港作为国际珠宝贸易中心的优势。她表示，在“一国两制”框架下，香港扮演着连接中国内地与海外市场的“超级联系人”和“超级增值者”角色。
洪指出，2026年首8个月，香港珠宝金银器出口同比增长逾47%至310亿美元，而珠宝进口则增长逾50%至400亿美元。在香港举行的两场国际珠宝展吸引了来自40多个国家和地区的约4,000家参展商。
她还介绍了2026年9月公布的香港第一个经济和社会发展五年规划（2026-2030年），以及香港行政长官的2026年施政报告。五年规划制定了巩固香港核心优势、推进国际金融中心、航运枢纽、贸易中心、航空枢纽、创新科技中心、全球高端人才聚集地“四中心一高地”发展的路线图。
洪表示，香港正在加快发展国际黄金交易市场，打造完善的珠宝贵金属产业生态系统。措施包括于2027年第一季度正式启动黄金中央清算结算系统，加强与上海黄金交易所的跨境互联互通。香港还设立黄金热线，为海外黄金交易商提供一站式支持，扩大黄金储存能力并提升提炼能力。
午餐会包括有关香港与新加坡珠宝市场趋势及合作机遇的小组讨论。午餐后，代表团与当地买家进行了一对一的商业配对会。
香港贸易发展局率领25名珠宝业界代表于11月10日至13日访问新加坡，与本地业界交流、了解市场趋势及探讨商机。

Hong Kong jewellery mission to Singapore touts trade hub role, growth
Hong Kong's trade office in Singapore co-hosted a business lunch for a jewellery delegation visiting via the Trade Connect platform. Officials highlighted record export growth, the city's role as a trade hub, and plans for a gold clearing system by Q1 2027.
Hong Kong’s Economic and Trade Office in Singapore co-hosted a business networking lunch on 11 November for a jewellery industry delegation visiting the city-state through the government’s “Trade Connect” platform. The lunch brought together about 80 business leaders, industry representatives and buyers from Hong Kong and Singapore.
In her speech, Office Director Polly Hung highlighted Hong Kong’s advantages as an international jewellery trading hub. She said Hong Kong plays the roles of “super-connector” and “super-value-adder” linking mainland China with overseas markets under the “one country, two systems” framework.
Hung noted that in the first eight months of 2026, Hong Kong’s exports of jewellery, goldware and silverware rose more than 47 per cent year on year to US$31 billion, while imports of jewellery rose more than 50 per cent to US$40 billion. Two international jewellery fairs held in Hong Kong attracted about 4,000 exhibitors from over 40 countries and regions.
She also introduced Hong Kong’s first five-year economic and social development plan (2026–2030), published in September 2026, and the 2026 policy address by the city’s chief executive. The five-year plan sets out a roadmap to consolidate Hong Kong’s core strengths and advance its development as the “four centres and one highland” – an international financial centre, shipping hub, trade centre, aviation hub, innovation and technology hub, and a global high-end talent pool.
Hung said Hong Kong is accelerating the development of an international gold trading market and building a comprehensive jewellery and precious-metals industry ecosystem. Measures include the formal launch of a gold central clearing and settlement system in the first quarter of 2027, and strengthening cross-border connectivity with the Shanghai Gold Exchange. Hong Kong is also setting up a gold hotline to provide one-stop support for overseas gold traders, expanding gold storage capacity and upgrading refining capabilities.
The lunch included a panel discussion on jewellery market trends and cooperation opportunities between Hong Kong and Singapore. After the lunch, the delegation held one-on-one business matching meetings with local buyers.
The Hong Kong Trade Development Council led a delegation of 25 jewellery industry representatives on a visit to Singapore from 10 to 13 November to exchange views with local industry players, learn about market trends and explore business opportunities.

content:
Nvidia Board Hires Former Prosecutor to Probe Jensen Huang's China Spy Scandal
Nvidia’s board hired a former federal prosecutor to investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a spy for China, as the company tries to manage the fallout of its scandal a week before its quarterly earnings report.
The Washington Post reports that the board brought in Joon H. Kim, a partner at the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to lead the investigation. Wachtell has handled sensitive inquiries before, including a probe into claims that the Los Angeles Clippers circumvented NBA salary rules in retaining Kawhi Leonard.
金担任检察官多年。 He worked in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York from 2000 to 2006 and again from 2013 to 2018, handling organized crime cases, including the murder prosecution of mobster Peter Gotti. In 2021, while in private practice, he was one of the independent investigators who examined sexual harassment allegations against former New York Governor Andrew M. Cuomo (D).
Huang disclosed the affair to employees in an email sent Sunday, the same day he told his wife. Breitbart News reported additional details that have come to light about Jensen’s partner in the affair, Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a spy for China:
Alice Huang 是中国官方媒体的前电视记者，在金融行业工作后于 2023 年加入 Megaspeed。当年 3 月至 11 月，新加坡的一份登记表将她列为公司董事。据《华尔街日报》此前报道，她于 2024 年 3 月在加利福尼亚州举行的 Nvidia 活动中首次见到黄仁勋，两人在台北鸡尾酒吧再次见面。 2025 年 5 月，在另一次访问台北期间，黄再次被拍到与她一起参加晚宴，两人亲吻脸颊并触摸手臂。
台北晚宴几周后，黄仁勋和英伟达高级游说者前往华盛顿会见副国务卿克里斯托弗·兰道(Christopher Landau)，认为政府应该批准为中国市场制造的 H20 芯片的出口许可证。几天后，黄与特朗普会面后，政府批准了 H20 的销售，以换取中国销售的 15% 归美国财政部。大约在同一时间，英伟达高管获悉政府对 Megaspeed 的调查。据报道，英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特联系了美国商务部工业与安全局局长杰弗里·凯斯勒。不久之后，司法部控制了 Megaspeed 探测器，削弱了商务部的作用。一些官员担心凯斯勒与英伟达的接触玷污了调查。
黄周一出现在英伟达圣克拉拉总部，像往常一样与高管举行例行早会。据接受 CNBC 采访的知情人士透露，当天晚些时候，在另一场闭门会议上，他直接谈到了此事并向员工道歉。他没有回答任何问题，然后继续今天的工作。周二，他回到办公室参加更多会议，距离英伟达公布季度收益还有一周。
英伟达股东对中国间谍丑闻作出反应，对该公司提起诉讼：
Schall, Brown & Schwartz律师事务所率先就英伟达中国间谍丑闻展开调查。随后罗森律师事务所提起了集体诉讼。

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia Board Hires Former Prosecutor to Probe Jensen Huang's China Spy Scandal
Nvidia’s board hired a former federal prosecutor to investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a spy for China, as the company tries to manage the fallout of its scandal a week before its quarterly earnings report.
The Washington Post reports that the board brought in Joon H. Kim, a partner at the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to lead the investigation. Wachtell has handled sensitive inquiries before, including a probe into claims that the Los Angeles Clippers circumvented NBA salary rules in retaining Kawhi Leonard.
Kim spent years as a prosecutor. He worked in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York from 2000 to 2006 and again from 2013 to 2018, handling organized crime cases, including the murder prosecution of mobster Peter Gotti. In 2021, while in private practice, he was one of the independent investigators who examined sexual harassment allegations against former New York Governor Andrew M. Cuomo (D).
Huang disclosed the affair to employees in an email sent Sunday, the same day he told his wife. Breitbart News reported additional details that have come to light about Jensen’s partner in the affair, Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a spy for China:
Alice Huang is a former television reporter for Chinese state media who joined Megaspeed in 2023 after working in the financial sector. A Singapore registration listed her as a company director from March to November that year. She first met Jensen Huang at an Nvidia event in California in March 2024, according to earlier Journal reporting, and the two met again at the Taipei cocktail bar. In May 2025, during another Taipei visit, Huang was photographed with her again at a dinner, the two seen kissing on the cheek and touching arms.
Weeks after the Taipei dinner, Huang and top Nvidia lobbyists traveled to Washington to meet with Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, arguing the government should approve export licenses for the H20 chip, which was built for the Chinese market. A few days later, after Huang met with Trump, the administration approved the H20 sale in exchange for 15 percent of China sales going to the U.S. Treasury. Around the same time, Nvidia executives learned of the government’s investigation into Megaspeed. Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, reportedly reached out to Jeffrey Kessler, head of the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security. Shortly afterward, the Justice Department took control of the Megaspeed probe, reducing the Commerce Department’s role. Some officials worried Kessler’s contact with Nvidia had tainted the investigation.
Huang showed up at Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters Monday and ran his regular morning meeting with top executives as usual. Later that day, in a separate closed-door meeting, he addressed the affair directly and apologized to staff, according to people familiar with the meeting who spoke to CNBC. He took no questions, then moved on to the day’s business. He was back in the office Tuesday for more meetings, one week before Nvidia reports quarterly earnings.
Nvidia shareholders have reacted to the China spy scandal by filing a lawsuit against the company:
The law firm of Schall, Brown & Schwartz was the first to launch an investigation of Nvidia over the Chinese spy scandal. The class-action lawsuit was then filed by the Rosen Law Firm.
The lawsuit claims Huang and Nvidia misled shareholders about the national security concerns the relationship raised, and that the omission artificially propped up Nvidia’s share price. “As a result of Defendants’ wrongful acts and omissions, and the precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities, Plaintiff and other Class members have suffered significant losses and damages,” the complaint states.
The mood inside the company has been mixed. One employee told CNBC the atmosphere was “sad,” while another described the response as “business as usual.”
Read more at the Washington Post here.
Lucas Nolan is a reporter for Breitbart News covering issues of AI, free speech, and online censorship.

在反情报简报会上，政府工作人员、军官和情报人员都被灌输了这样一句话：“如果她是 10 分，而你是 5 分，那么她就是间谍！”或者，正如美国陆军反情报司令部在情人节发布的那样：“不需要数学家就能算出‘10 + 5 = 美人计’。”这个非常漂亮的女人突然对你平凡的存在感兴趣，可能别有用心，这就是信息。
黄仁勋的生活肯定不是典型的——他是一位亿万富翁，是 Nvidia 虚张声势的首席执行官，Nvidia 是 21 世纪最热门、最具地缘政治影响力的公司之一。他当然意识到自己有可能与情报人员发生冲突。事实上，很难想象世界上有多少公司会成为外国情报机构更优先的目标。
所有这些都使得本周震动股市的消息更加令人惊讶。黄是如何卷入一场将不忠、国际间谍活动、特朗普政府和价值数万亿美元的人工智能行业的经济庞然大物混合在一起的间谍丑闻的？
故事从万圣节前夕开始，《纽约时报》刊登了一篇六行文章，报道称黄是中国间谍阴谋的目标。据称，从 2024 年到 2025 年期间开始，黄与 Alice Huang（无亲属关系）有染，后者曾是新加坡一家名为 Megaspeed 的云提供商的高管。美国情报机构警告美国高级官员，他们认为她是中国情报人员。到目前为止，已经启动调查的英伟达董事会表示，“没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密遭到泄露”，但这远不是唯一的担忧。
正如人们所预料的那样，中国否认有任何以黄仁勋为中心的邪恶阴谋。中国外交部发言人周一表示，“所谓中国间谍的说法完全是无端猜测，纯属污蔑抹黑”。
但据《纽约时报》和《金融时报》报道，美国情报官员还声称，黄乐（又名黄乐）正在向中国国家安全部情报机构汇报工作。周一，Megaspeed 在 LinkedIn 上表示，美国当局“没有发现任何涉及非法转让芯片或任何非法活动的证据”。 （到目前为止，没有任何迹象表明曾任中国国家记者的黄爱丽是中国情报部门的雇员或“官员”；她被认为是一个“资产”，一个为情报机构提供帮助的局外人，有时是为了报酬，有时不是。）

【原文 English Original】
China’s Nvidia Honeypot Isn’t Surprising. Jensen Huang Fell for It Anyway | WIRED
There’s a specific mantra drilled into government workers, military officers, and intelligence personnel during counterintelligence briefings: “If she’s a 10 and you’re a 5, she’s a spy!” Or, as the US Army’s Counterintelligence Command posted on Valentine’s Day: “It doesn’t take a mathematician to figure out ‘10 + 5 = honeytrap.’” The very beautiful woman who is suddenly interested in your very ordinary existence probably has ulterior motives, is the message.
Jensen Huang surely doesn’t live a typical life—he’s a centibillionaire, the swashbuckling CEO of Nvidia, one of the hottest and most geopolitically consequential companies of the 21st century. Surely he’s aware of the possibility that he’d cross paths with intelligence assets. In fact, it’s hard to think of many companies in the world that would be a higher priority target for foreign intelligence agencies.
All of that makes the stock-shaking news this week all the more surprising. How did Huang get embroiled in a spy scandal that mixes infidelity, international espionage, the Trump administration, and the economic behemoth of the multitrillion-dollar AI industry?
The story kicked off just before Halloween, with a six-byline story in The New York Times reporting that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Starting somewhere between 2024 and 2025, Huang allegedly had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a one-time executive at a Singapore-based cloud provider known as Megaspeed. US intelligence agencies warned top US officials that they believed she was a Chinese intelligence asset. So far, Nvidia’s board, which has launched its own investigation, says it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that’s far from the only concern.
As one would expect, China has denied any nefarious plot centered on Jensen Huang. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson on Monday said, “The narrative about so-called Chinese spies is entirely based on groundless speculation—it’s nothing more than slander and smearing.”
But according to reporting by The New York Times and the Financial Times, US intelligence officials also claim that Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was reporting to China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency. On Monday, Megaspeed said on LinkedIn that US authorities found “no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities." (There’s no indication so far that Alice Huang, a one-time Chinese state journalist, is an employee or “officer” of Chinese intelligence; she’s believed to be an “asset,” an outsider who aids an intelligence agency, sometimes for pay, sometimes not.)
China, though, has elevated economic espionage to a core pillar of its economic and military development, stealing the designs for everything from US fighter jets to solar panels and commercial paint recipes. “Honeypots” or “honey traps”—positioning an alluring operative to seduce or develop a relationship with a key target—are one of intelligence’s most infamous and well-established strategies. French officials have warned specifically about Chinese honeypots since at least 2011, when intelligence reports cited a pharmaceutical researcher who was seduced and then blackmailed by a Chinese spy operation.
Over the past quarter of a century, as Silicon Valley emerged as a center of political and economic power, it has become a key focus of Chinese intelligence. In one plot, a Chinese national named Fang Fang spent years trying to cozy up to Bay Area politicians, including then US Representative Eric Swalwell. (While intelligence officials at the time reportedly believed Fang to be an operative, law enforcement officials never brought any charges against her). When traveling to China, US business executives have become accustomed to leaving their regular phones and computers at home and using burner devices to prevent the installation of spyware or malware (as I did, when I traveled to China for WIRED in 2019 to report on Huawei). In 2012, when Leon Panetta was making his first trip to China as defense secretary, he and his team were advised to bathe and shower in the dark in the event his hotel room was bugged. Last year, the threat of honeypots prompted the US government to explicitly ban personnel working in China and Hong Kong from engaging in romantic or sexual relationships with Chinese citizens. More recently, US officials joined with allies to warn about China’s increasingly sophisticated “LinkedIn espionage”: using the business-focused social networking site to recruit and build relationships with unwitting executives.
Alice Huang’s Megaspeed, for its part, is a major Pacific region player in cloud services focused on the advanced computer chips that are the heart of Nvidia’s business. The Biden administration had sharply limited the export of cutting-edge chips globally to slow China’s development of AI, but Jensen Huang has successfully lobbied the Trump administration to loosen those restrictions.
Speaking at a press conference on Monday, Donald Trump denied having prior knowledge of Alice Huang’s potential espionage. “I didn’t hear about it then, but a lot of people have heard about it, and Jensen totally denies that,” Trump said. “I asked him that question: ‘Did you have any idea that she was a spy?’ He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy.’” On Tuesday, the Times reported that Marco Rubio had briefed Trump in May, right before Jensen Huang joined the president on Air Force One for a trip to China.
The veracity of Trump's claims will surely be investigated, especially in the context of the famous Watergate maxim: “What did the president know and when did he know it?” Nvidia’s CEO has been publicly linked to the Megaspeed executive since at least 2024 and Alice’s husband, Kang Weigh, has reportedly known Jensen since the 2010s. WIRED’s Lauren Goode reported on Monday that Jensen Huang, starting in 2025, hired Risa Heller’s crisis communications firm, which is well-versed in handling public sex scandals. This spring, secretary of state Marco Rubio evidently helped craft a classified memo inside the administration warning officials about Jensen Huang’s potentially compromising relationship.
Jensen Huang—who has developed an important reputation as AI’s number one cheerleader at the frontier of AI labs—is now stuck in an awkward situation. Is he an idiot, unaware that his paramour might have been a foreign intelligence asset? Merely reckless with his own reputation, fiduciary responsibility to Nvidia, and the technological security of the United States? Or a witting accomplice to undermining US national security?
Regardless of the truth, Nvidia loses. Shareholders have ridden a roller-coaster that has seen Nvidia’s stock rise by about 600 percent over the past five years, becoming the world’s second-most valuable company. In the past month, the stock has plummeted by a quarter. The disaster for Nvidia is just beginning, it seems, as lawsuits loom, including by its own shareholders.
Similarly, the Trump administration is likely to face real questions from the newly Democratic congress: When were the president and other top officials briefed about this intelligence threat? What communication, if any, did they make to Nvidia and to whom? Should more have been done by US intelligence to block Alice Huang from having access to Nvidia and its CEO?
The fact that Megaspeed is a major customer of Nvidia makes everything more complicated. Indeed, reports have circulated for at least a year that the US was concerned that Megaspeed was diverting chips to Chinese intelligence agencies, an allegation that could have massive consequences for the global AI race. Bloomberg this week reported that Megaspeed's subsidiaries have purchased billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips and that an audit requested by the US government last year found that Megaspeed couldn’t initially account for some 50,000 chips it had purchased.
Meanwhile, Nvidia’s Huang and President Trump developed a uniquely close professional relationship. They’ve met multiple times as Huang has pushed to loosen Biden-era export controls, which Trump has repeatedly relaxed; Huang has donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom project; while en route to Beijing earlier this year with a delegation of tech leaders, including Elon Musk and Tim Cook, Trump’s Air Force One actually made a special stop in Alaska to pick up Huang; Huang also attended a White House state dinner for Chinese president Xi Jinping and Trump, who in turn, awarded him a National Medal of Science earlier this fall.
The implication that Trump knew and did nothing for a year would make this one of the greatest counterintelligence failures of the past decade. There will be consequences: Across history, many have gone to prison for honeypot scandals; a former adviser was arrested just last year in a similar plot; though he was acquitted of committing economic espionage, he was convicted for making false statements to investigators.
Even in normal circumstances, corporate America’s tolerance of CEO misbehavior has shrunken dramatically. In recent years, CEOs at companies as varied as Nestlé, Kohl’s, BP, NBCUniversal, and the railroad Norfolk Southern have all resigned or been forced out after inappropriate relationships that violated company standards.
If Nvidia were any other company and Jensen Huang any other CEO, the facts of the scandal currently known would be enough to topple some heads. But Trump is still president, and November is only a third over. It’s not even clear that this will rank as the biggest scandal of the month—but it should.

content:
Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case
Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser.
What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.
（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）
With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.
（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）
In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.
（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）
Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.
（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。）
Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States.
（多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。）
Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.
（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）
After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.
（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。）
Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.
（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）
He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.
（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。）
The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.
（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）
We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.
（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）
The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.
（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。）
With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community.
（您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）
Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese:
https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole
(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)
（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）
http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641
(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears of the Goddess of Liberty and Red Dog. Qi is the Chairwoman of the Women Writers committee, Independent Chinese PEN Center.)
（作者/齊家貞，流亡作家，著有系列傳記《自由神的眼泪──父女两代囚徒的真實故事》（後改名《黑牆裡的倖存者》和《紅狗：—個被釋女囚的真實故事》在香港和台灣出版。齊家貞曾先後擔任國際筆會獨立中文筆會理事會理事、副會長、秘書長等職務，並在澳洲建立了“齊氏文化基金會”，每年頒發“推動中國進步獎”截至2019年已連續頒獎12屆。）
https://liuvswei.blogspot.com/2020/08/metoo.html
(by Lau Kayee, Chairwoman of Network for Women In Politics, Hong Kong; Spokeswoman of Hong Kong Civil Human Rights Front.)
（作者/劉家儀，香港婦女參政網絡主席，六四新生代秘書長，支聯會常委，香港市民捍衛人權陣線發言人。）
With your contributions, we will be able to set a positive example for #MeToo victims by raising awareness about women’s and children's rights, globally.
因您的資助，我們將能夠為#MeToo運動傷害者們建立一個積極的個案，為提高女性及孩童的權利意識而有所貢獻。

content:
Fundraiser by Boston Standswithhk : US Hong Kong Safe Harbor Postcard Campaign
Boston Standswithhk is organizing this fundraiser.
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***
While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.
11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。
In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):
鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):
The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)
《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)
The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)
《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)
In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!
在上一次推動《香港人權與民主法》的明信片運動中，我們向國會送出了超過3000張的明信片。我們不是任何正式組織的成員，也沒有運營資金，所以我們竭誠呼籲您為我們提供資金，並幫助我們將這些明信片送交您們所屬的國會議員，提醒他們香港的緊急狀況，並呼籲他們立即採取行動。所有受到的捐款將支持我們的打印和交付成本。萬分感謝！
