【原文 English Original】
AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
Ravie LakshmananNov 11, 2026Artificial Intelligence / Web Security
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a campaign in which an emerging agentic penetration testing platform called AntiFox has been used to steal Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials and pivot laterally into compromised environments.
"In several recently observed intrusions, Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces were associated with confirmed malicious actions against internet-facing web services and associated AWS environments," Arctic Wolf Labs said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
The activity has been observed chaining together web exploitation and web shell deployment to facilitate configuration discovery, credential validation, cloud-service enumeration, secret access, and storage operations.
AntiFox, available for download from GitHub, has been described as an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven autonomous penetration testing platform. As of writing, the project has been forked 251 times and starred 474 times.
On its README page, the project maintainer states -
Given an authorized target, a planner / worker / main-agent multi-agent system runs the full engagement over a dual-graph core (a global asset graph + a per-task exploration graph) — recon → attack-surface discovery → exploitation → finding capture → report delivery — fully observable, interactive, and deliverable
Unlike most automated pentest tools that are "great at discovery, but stop at discovery," AntiFox puts its weight on delivery — turning what the AI finds into a report that an engineer can understand, reproduce, back with evidence, and hand straight to the client.
According to Arctic Wolf, some of the initial access activity is associated with a compromised internet-facing Internet Information Services (IIS) application. The access is then leveraged to create an ASPX web shell using "w3wp.exe," the IIS worker process, and run operating system commands to perform the following actions -
Run PowerShell commands to locate web.config files and configuration backups
Read application settings and database connection strings
Enumerate debug and error-log directories
Attempts to connect to an internal production database using a credential extracted from the application configuration
Copy configuration and log files into a web-accessible upload directory
"On a compromised IIS server, commands run through w3wp.exe identified the execution context with whoami, enumerated the application directory, checked permissions with icacls, and tested the ability to write files into the web root," Arctic Wolf said.
"The creation of an ASPX web shell by w3wp.exe, followed by command execution through the same IIS worker process, suggests compromise through the affected web application."
The precise vulnerability used to achieve code execution on the IIS server is not known. In other attacks, the threat actor is said to have started with a valid AWS credential obtained through as-yet-undetermined means.
Specifically, this involved abusing valid IAM identities to validate credentials and enumerate dozens of services, including IAM, EC2, S3, Lambda, Secrets Manager, KMS, RDS, ECS, EKS, Redshift, Athena, Glue, Systems Manager, API Gateway, CloudWatch, CloudFormation, DynamoDB, and Amazon Bedrock.
While a majority of these authenticated cross-service API requests ended up with an "AccessDenied" error, some of the discovery and secret-access operations were successful, according to the cybersecurity company.
In at least some instances, the activity has been observed progressing beyond Secrets Manager enumeration to a successful GetSecretValue request against a production secret. Elsewhere, a valid AWS identity was used for S3 discovery and object operations via API calls.
"Agentic frameworks such as these make penetration testing techniques more accessible to threat actors, while increasing the speed and consistency with which these techniques can be applied in live attacks," Arctic Wolf said.
The disclosure comes as threat actors are increasingly weaponizing AI-powered penetration testing tools like ARTEX to conduct broad-scale attacks across the world, enabling them to automate various stages of an intrusion with minimal human intervention.
The integration of AI has allowed adversaries, both large and small, to adapt established tradecraft and deploy them at machine speed, making it possible to progress from scanning GitHub for secrets to exfiltrating data from an Azure Key Vault in five minutes.
Earlier this week, VECERT disclosed details of a campaign dubbed Operation Ghost-Campus orchestrated by a Chinese threat actor that uses AI agents to maintain perpetual, cost-free access to large language models (LLMs) and eventually perform automated academic fraud and steal data belonging to over 5,000 students enrolled at the Fengxian Campus.
"The agent industrializes the creation of accounts on the search engine fofa.info, scans the global cyberspace for misconfigured servers, extracts API keys for OpenAI and DeepSeek, automatically verifies their financial balances, and injects them into the attacker's development environment," VECERT said.
"This stolen computing power fuels an interactive GoTTY terminal ('Pi — AI Coding Assistant') and, by extension, provides intelligence to the scripts that sustain academic fraud bots ('heartbeat' bots) and extractors of financial data and personally identifiable information (PII) belonging to thousands of students at the Fengxian Campus."
According to data from Censys, there are 1,465 hosts running an exposed ARTEX console as of November 4, 2026, with most of them located in the U.S., Hong Kong, China, Japan, Singapore, and South Korea. However, it's worth noting that not every instance is necessarily malicious in nature.
In a separate report, Check Point Research said it identified 2,557 systems that hosted ARTEX, including 10 misconfigured instances exposing their full databases.
"In many observed cases, ARTEX required remarkably little interaction from its operators once an objective had been established," Check Point said. "Rather than continuously directing attacks step by step, operators frequently issued a goal and left the agent fleet to work toward it. Human interactions were largely limited to checking progress, asking whether a target had been compromised or occasionally adjusting priorities."
The vast majority of the attacks are designed to siphon cryptocurrency, steal Apple code-signing certificates, compromise gaming accounts, and conduct denial-of-service (DoS) attacks against gambling websites. The activity has been found to exploit vulnerabilities related to weak or hard-coded passwords, missing authentication, insecure direct object references, and remote code execution.
In the campaign targeting Apple code-signing certificates, ARTEX agents searched compromised systems for certificate databases, followed by validating the stolen certificates by checking passwords, private keys, Apple revocation status, expiration dates, and associated provisioning profiles.
Ultimately, the activity is estimated to have harvested more than 300 certificates and their passwords, out of which three certificates passed the full validation process and could be used to sign arbitrary iOS applications.
The biggest change brought by agentic hacking to the cyber threat landscape is scale and speed, Check Point cautioned, as a cybercriminal with limited technical skills can task AI agents with investigating a number of targets in parallel and exploiting them using known and zero-day vulnerabilities with less manual effort.
"Its relevance to us lies in its scale, speed and persistence," CERT-EU said in an alert. "ARTEX can test large numbers of low-complexity misconfigurations, including those a human tester would notice but not have time to check, and it can work through long attack chains without the fatigue that limits manual testing."
"The same is true of complex payload crafting. Exploitation paths that need carefully tailored payloads often take more effort than the severity of the finding justifies, so a manual assessment may leave them untested."
Tools like AntiFox and ARTEX are part of a broader set of about 45 open-source agentic attack frameworks that are engineered to connect to an LLM and can act on outputs autonomously. They fall under five broad categories -
Network kill chain capable of end-to-end reconnaissance, exploitation, and post-exploitation: PentAGI, RedAmon, and DarkMoon
Web-app and API: Strix, Shannon, and PentestGPT
C2-integrated: Sage, echidna, Pojun, and FORANG
Harnesses: RAPTOR, CyberStrike, cyber-harness, Nebula and Cybermes
Research prototypes: Incalmo, hackingBuddyGPT, VulnBot, HackSynth, AutoPT, and Ares
"Each framework has public source code and wires a model into a loop that runs tools and acts on their output," GitGuardian said.
"Agentic AI pentesting tools hand their agent a shell and web access, so the model can assemble a pipeline at runtime. A GitHub search, a scanner download, and a found key passed to the next call are all one prompt away, even though none of it ships in the repository."

content:
CoreWeave 盈利上涨提振 AI 云股和 Nvidia中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 12 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
CoreWeave 盈利上涨提振人工智能云股票和 Nvidia
强劲的盈利缓解了对人工智能泡沫的担忧，周三 CoreWeave 股价上涨 10%。尽管业界对数据中心监管和软银 37 亿美元的减记感到担忧，但英伟达和其他云股票的上涨提振了股票。
2026 年 11 月 11 日 21:29 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 12 日 04:25 · 阅读时间 2 分钟
CoreWeave 周三上涨 10%，引发了遭受重创的人工智能云股票的上涨，因为该公司的巨额支出带来了强劲的收入增长，而且该公司发出信号，表示将从引发人工智能泡沫警报的借贷狂潮中回落。该财报还使 CoreWeave 的主要支持者英伟达 (Nvidia) 的股价上涨了 5%，此前该公司首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 与一名被指控为北京间谍的中国女商人发生恋情，引发了对该公司未来的担忧，导致该公司股价连续两天大幅下跌。
Nebius 和 Iren 等所谓的“新云”公司的股价在经历了数周的动荡后出现上涨，原因是人们担心，如果人工智能需求放缓，这些公司债务驱动的数据中心扩张可能会适得其反。上周民主党中期选举的大获全胜对该行业造成了又一次打击，几位获胜的候选人呼吁加强监管并暂停新数据中心的建设，包括在德克萨斯州的关键市场。
CoreWeave首席执行官Michael Intrator周二对路透社表示，更严格的审查可能会减缓整个行业的数据中心建设速度，但他预计这不会显着改变公司的扩张计划或推高成本。该公司还上调了年度收入预测，并表示，在近期借贷成本飙升后，不会利用无担保债务市场，现有合同的现金流将覆盖当前和未来的债务偿还。
以麦迪逊·雷扎伊 (Madison Rezaei) 为首的伯恩斯坦分析师在一份客户报告中表示：“CoreWeave 的季度表现是我们所要求的最好的。统计数据从优秀到卓越，资金问题得到解决，战略举措也有意义。”但他们警告说，当人工智能计算能力的紧缩得到缓解时，CoreWeave“将成为首当其冲、也是最严重的打击之一”。
周二，随着软银对其美国数据中心供电设备的不可退还付款进行了 37 亿美元的减记，人工智能投资时机错误的风险变得显而易见。这导致这家日本科技投资者第二季度净亏损达 70 亿美元，这是近两年来的首次。
目前，CoreWeave 的业绩让人工智能基础设施股的投资者有理由欢呼，Nebius、Iren、Oracle 和 Applied Digital 在盘前交易中股价上涨了 4.7% 至 11.8%。截至周二，除 Nebius 之外的所有股票今年以来均下跌了 32% 至 48%，而 Nebius 则飙升了 60%。包括 CoreWeave 在内的云公司当天的市值预计将超过 250 亿美元，而如果涨幅保持不变，仅 Nvidia 一家公司的市值就将增加约 2100 亿美元。 Nebius 将于周四开盘前报告业绩。

CoreWeave earnings rally lifts AI cloud stocks and Nvidia | China Labour Bulletin Board
Thursday, 12 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
CoreWeave earnings rally lifts AI cloud stocks and Nvidia
CoreWeave shares jumped 10 per cent on Wednesday after strong earnings eased AI bubble fears. The rally lifted Nvidia and other cloud stocks, despite industry concerns over data centre regulation and SoftBank's US$3.7 billion writedown.
11 Nov 2026 at 21:29 HKT · updated 12 Nov, 04:25 · 2 min read
CoreWeave jumped 10 per cent on Wednesday, igniting a rally in battered AI cloud stocks, as its hefty spending yielded strong revenue growth and the company signalled a pullback from the borrowing binge that had set off alarms of an AI bubble. The earnings also lifted shares of key CoreWeave backer Nvidia by 5 per cent, after a bruising two-day slide driven by worries about CEO Jensen Huang's future at the company following his affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.
Shares of so-called "neoclouds" including Nebius and Iren rallied after facing weeks of turmoil on fears that their debt-fuelled data centre expansion could backfire if AI demand slows. The Democratic midterm sweep last week dealt another blow to the industry, with several winning candidates campaigning for tighter regulation and moratoriums on new data centre construction, including in the crucial market of Texas.
CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told Reuters on Tuesday that greater scrutiny could slow data centre construction across the industry, but he did not expect it to significantly alter the company's expansion plans or drive up costs. The company also raised its annual revenue forecast and said it would not tap unsecured debt markets after a recent spike in borrowing costs and that cash flow from existing contracts would cover both current and future debt repayments.
"CoreWeave delivered about the best quarter we could have asked for. Stats were good-to-great, funding concerns were addressed and the strategic moves make sense," Bernstein analysts led by Madison Rezaei said in a client note. But they warned that CoreWeave "will be among the first and hardest hit" when the crunch in AI computing capacity eases.
The risks of mistiming AI investments became evident on Tuesday as SoftBank took a US$3.7 billion writedown on non-refundable payments for equipment to power its US data centres. That pushed the Japanese tech investor to a second-quarter net loss of US$7 billion, its first in nearly two years.
For now, CoreWeave's results gave investors in AI infrastructure stocks reason to cheer, with Nebius, Iren, Oracle and Applied Digital climbing between 4.7 per cent and 11.8 per cent in premarket trading. All the stocks but Nebius have lost 32 per cent to 48 per cent this year as of Tuesday, while Nebius has surged 60 per cent. Together, the cloud companies, including CoreWeave, were set to gain more than US$25 billion in market value on the day, while Nvidia alone stood to add about US$210 billion, if gains hold. Nebius is due to report results before Thursday's opening bell.

香港兴业国际与SCP集团合作浙江综合体项目
香港兴业国际与万科旗下SCP集团签署战略合作协议，共同管理浙江嘉兴“绣湖兴业印象城”综合体项目。项目总建筑面积约23万平方米，预计破土动工
香港兴业国际与万科旗下印力集团签订战略合作协议，共同运营管理浙江嘉兴“秀湖兴业印象城”综合体项目。两家公司还表达了在中国大陆地区进行长期、全面战略合作的意向。
该项目由公司与嘉兴运河湾城市投资集团共同开发。总建筑面积约23万平方米。项目预计今年开工，预计2029年开业。项目建成后，香港兴业国际与SCP集团将共同管理该项目的商业运营，将引入300多个品牌。
香港兴业国际表示，该项目标志着公司向轻资产管理战略转变的新里程碑。两家公司将继续围绕长三角和粤港澳大湾区核心城市群，在商业资产投资开发、存量资产运营及价值提升等领域探索潜在的合作机会。

The project, with total floor area of about 230,000 square metres, is expected to break groun
Hong Kong兴业国际 (Hong Kong兴业 International) has entered into a strategic co-operation agreement with 印力集团 (SCP Group), a subsidiary of China Vanke, to jointly operate and manage the "秀湖兴业印象城" (Xiuhu Xingye Impression City) mixed-use project in Jiaxing, Zhejiang province. The two companies also expressed an intention for long-term and comprehensive strategic co-operation across mainland China.
The project is being jointly developed by the company and the Jiaxing运河湾 City Investment Group. It will have a total floor area of approximately 230,000 square metres. Construction is scheduled to begin this year, with the project expected to open in 2029. Upon completion, Hong Kong兴业 International and SCP Group will jointly manage the commercial operations of the project, which will introduce more than 300 brands.
Hong Kong兴业 International stated that the project marks a new milestone in the company's shift towards an asset-light management strategy. The two companies will continue to explore potential co-operation opportunities in commercial asset investment and development, existing asset operations and value enhancement, focusing on the core city clusters of the Yangtze River Delta and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area.

|黄仁勋事件暴露硅谷国家安全力量
黄仁勋事件暴露硅谷国家安全实力
中期选举的蓝色海啸刚刚登陆，特朗普政府就遭遇了另一场危机。
11月8日，黄仁勋承认（在新窗口中打开）恋情。据《纽约时报》报道，美国情报机构得出结论，他的情妇是中国国家安全部的情报人员。
此事的消息震惊了市场和监管机构。黄领导的英伟达是全球最有价值的公司，为西方与中国的技术竞争提供核心技术。他与美国政治机构关系密切，今年早些时候，他与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起乘坐空军一号对北京进行国事访问。
黄的事件显示了华盛顿与硅谷关系核心的新矛盾。私营企业高管比以往任何时候都拥有更大的权力，而旨在保护美国国家安全的机构却没有适应这种变化。
国家安全机构的设立是为了保护敏感信息。它们还保护政府决策者免受影响力的影响。针对黄的威胁集中在中国可能影响英伟达向中国出售人工智能芯片的立场，而不是控制任何特定的机密信息。
美国主要科技公司的领导人正在成为美国国家安全政策的结构性决定性人物。
世界各国政府每天都有理由将黄仁勋这样的人视为关键的地缘政治人物。
9 月，五角大楼任命 SpaceX 和特斯拉首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 Anduril Industries 创始人帕尔默·拉基 (Palmer Luckey) 以及前众议院议长纽特·金里奇 (Newt Gingrich) 为 Project Meridian 的领导者。这三人将指导美国战争的未来，包括采购数千亿美元的装备。
2025 年 12 月，黄仁勋本人对 CSIS 表示，“我们国家非凡的科技产业是我们国家安全的一部分”。他的公司控制着全球 80-85% 的人工智能芯片硬件市场（在新窗口中打开），通过对基础设施的控制，将自己定位为美国实力的先锋。
硅谷高管给自己的任务是塑造美国的国家安全利益，而不是满足政府的要求，从而影响世界如何看待美国的实力。

Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
Trump knew about Huang’s Chinese contact months before the public did, and Washington has no rulebook for cases like it.

|Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
The blue tsunami of the midterms had barely landed onshore when yet another crisis hit the Trump administration.
On 8 November, Jensen Huang admitted (Opens in new window) to an affair. American intelligence agencies, according (Opens in new window) to the New York Times, have concluded that his mistress is an intelligence asset for China’s Ministry of State Security.
News of the affair shocked markets and regulators. Huang leads Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company that provides the core technology for the West’s technological competition with China. He is deeply tied with the American political apparatus, flying on Air Force One with President Donald Trump for his state visit to Beijing earlier in the year.
Huang’s affair shows a new contradiction at the heart of Washington’s relationship to Silicon Valley. Private executives have more power than ever, while the institutions designed to protect America’s national security haven’t adapted to that change.
National security apparatuses are set up to protect sensitive information. They also protect government decision-makers from influence efforts. The threat against Huang centred on the potential for China to influence Nvidia’s position on selling AI chips to China, rather than control of any particular item of classified information.
The leaders of major American technology firms are becoming structurally decisive figures in American national security policy.
Governments around the world gain reasons every day to treat people like Jensen Huang as key geopolitical figures.
In September, the Pentagon named (Opens in new window) SpaceX and Tesla chief Elon Musk and Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey, alongside former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich, as the leaders of Project Meridian. The three will guide the future of American warfare, including acquisition of hundreds of billions of dollars of equipment.
In December 2025, Huang himself told (Opens in new window) CSIS, “our nation’s extraordinary technology industry is part of our national security”. His company, which controls 80–85% of the global market (Opens in new window) for AI chip hardware, positions itself at the vanguard of American power through its grip on the infrastructure.
Silicon Valley executives are giving themselves the job of shaping America’s national security interests rather than delivering what the government requests – in turn influencing how the world sees American power.
US President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman speak with Elon Musk, Jensen Huang and other business leaders at the US-Saudi Investment Forum, 19 November 2025, at the John F. Kennedy Centre for the Performing Arts in Washington, DC (Daniel Torok/Official White House Photo)
When Musk throttled Starlink access to Ukraine’s soldiers, speculation abounded about who authorised the slowdown between Musk or Trump. The question itself proved the point, that critical decisions may be made on either side of the sector wall.
In Brazil’s presidential election, thousands of protestors gathered outside of Meta’s Sao Paolo office to decry what they saw as the company meddling in their election. In the months prior, the President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign released evidence (Opens in new window) that Meta’s platforms were promoting his opponent’s campaign and limiting Lula’s ability to reach voters. Meta accepted the result but denied any political intention behind it. The reputational damage had been done: a majority of Brazilians believe that American technology poses a risk to their national security.
A Silicon Valley executive who controls technology used by military and intelligence services may not have access to classified information, but can make consequential decisions about how the technology operates.
These companies, deeply tied to the Trump White House and at the vanguard of its definition of American power, are producing consequences that have a significance that rivals that of entire governments.
Governments around the world gain reasons every day to treat people like Jensen Huang as key geopolitical figures. This scandal shows that counterintelligence services need to account for that reality.
The FBI, the key counterintelligence service in the United States, has some efforts in place to protect private industry. They investigate attempts by foreign governments to infiltrate critical companies. Their goal is to protect classified information and hardware that could be stolen and repurposed.
As the public role that these executives play changes, so too does the problem of counterintelligence defence. A Silicon Valley executive who controls the technology used by military and intelligence services around the world may not themselves have access to classified information, but they can make consequential decisions about how the technology operates. These decisions could change what a country is capable of doing, or what technology an adversary is able to access.
Beyond the question of the appropriate counterintelligence protection for figures like Huang, there also comes the question of their political relationships.
Well before the public was made aware, Trump was informed (Opens in new window) about Huang’s relationship, including the intelligence community’s assessment that his mistress was tied to Chinese intelligence. Even after those briefings, Trump continued to speak with Huang and, once the scandal was revealed, publicly defended him.
Even once counterintelligence services adapt to the moving future, they can always be countermanded by chief executives who make political calculations about figures. Trump could have pushed Huang out, but in doing so would have alienated a key political ally, someone central to his strategic competition with China. Huang’s embrace of MAGA has also been helpful to Trump in building a political and economic support base in Silicon Valley.
The decision to do nothing with the information developed by the FBI was a political one, made because Trump saw Huang as indispensable.
This dynamic matters for every country that relies on American technology in both its civilian and public sectors. These new vulnerabilities will not stop at American borders.
The new generation of leaders taking centre stage in the United States must grapple with the seemingly insurmountable power that Silicon Valley has accumulated in the Trump era. Backlash to that very group was part of the substantial rebuke delivered by voters.
In governing, these new leaders from both parties will have to reimagine national security – including counterintelligence – to cover the public power now wielded by private actors.
Cory Alpert is a PhD researcher at the University of Melbourne, where he studies the impact of AI on democracy. Previously, he served in the Biden White House for three years and as the senior adviser to Mayor Steve Benjamin.

content:
Fundraiser by Lori Engel : Lift Lori's Load
Lori’s fund covers neurological care, nutrition, vital daily needs, and her service dog
Lori Engel is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Lori Engel. I’m 59, homebound in Oregon. I live completely alone with life-altering neurological injuries and disabilities that have reshaped every part of my world.
I grew up as a missionary child in Brazil, where faith, service, and compassion became the foundation of my life. As an adult, I carried that forward—serving six years as a missionary teacher in Taiwan, then eleven years as a chaplain, walking alongside people in illness, grief, crisis, and loss. Caring for others wasn’t just my work; it was my identity. The last two years of my career, I was the Director of Chaplain Services for a healthcare organization.
Prior to becoming a chaplain, I was an English teacher for almost two decades, teaching both in Taiwan and at universities in the U.S.
That path shifted profoundly starting in late 2006. Over time, I sustained multiple traumatic brain injuries and a toxic reaction to Cipro that damaged my nerves and muscles. I developed serious neurological conditions, including cerebellar damage, ataxia, polyneuropathy, spasticity, severe balance impairment, swallowing difficulties, and vision disturbances, to name a few. These affect my ability to walk, stand, use my arms consistently, regulate my nervous system, or handle even basic daily tasks.
Despite these initial injuries, I continued working as a chaplain until 2015, pushing through pain and limitations to serve others, through God's grace and the aid of nutraceuticals. Additional neurological injuries in 2015 made it impossible to continue, leaving me homebound ever since, unable to drive.
Here is a brief summary of all my injuries:
My injuries consist of multiple TBIs (traumatic brain injury) from falling backward onto the kitchen tile floor, hitting the back of my head; slamming my forehead into a concrete bunk bed; and falling and hitting the side of my head here in Oregon. I also experienced medical malpractice that damaged my cervical spine. I was erroneously prescribed fluroquinolones Avelox and Cipro for 30 days straight, which severely damaged my nerves and tendons. (The FDA has issued warnings about these drugs.) Then I got a bad infection. Later, I also experienced thermal burns to my spine and base of my head.
Then, I was exposed to and living in wildfires so severe that ashes were all around me here in Oregon in 2020, which exponentially exacerbated all my autonomic, nerve, and vascular damage, as well as breathing. Then in 2021 I had Covid, which causes neurological issues in even healthy people. For me, it created additional issues.
There has been a compounded, cumulative effect of all the layered injuries. Most people struggle to comprehend such a parade of horribles, but I do have records.
It has been more than I can ever put into words. I am just thankful to be alive. I am thankful for the many years I worked as a chaplain, until there were just too many injuries.
Simple things most people take for granted—opening a package, standing at the sink, stepping outside, or even too much visual input—can overload my fragile system, causing loss of balance, neurological shutdown, or crushing exhaustion. Some days I can’t get out of bed. Others, I push through just to care for myself and my faithful dog Teddie, only to crash afterward.
I haven’t seen my family in 13 years (they live on the East Coast), and for the last 10-plus years I can’t travel. I receive no family financial support. The isolation is profound, and Teddie—my constant companion, emotional anchor, and service companion in many ways—is one of the biggest reasons I keep going, in addition to God's miraculous care.
Yet every day, I fight to heal and hold onto as much independence as possible. As my health allows, I write devotional pieces that integrate faith, neuroscience, and psychology—sharing insights on resilience, hope, and spiritual growth on social media. It’s a small but meaningful way I continue to give back and encourage others, even from home.
My lifeline is an intensive, carefully managed regimen: specialized therapies, targeted nutrition, and essential supplements that stabilize my brain, muscles, emotions, and overall functioning. When I can stay consistent with these protocols, I feel more like myself—steadier, clearer, hopeful. When I can’t, everything declines quickly: neurologically, physically, and emotionally.
My disability income is severely limited (SSDI), and it does not even cover rent. Ongoing costs far exceed what I can cover. Neurological medications/nutraceuticals alone are expensive and not covered by Medicare. I also need nutritious food tailored to my conditions, basic utilities, in-home support, and care for Teddie.
I’m not asking for luxuries—only the basics that allow me to continue healing, stay safe at home, avoid further decline, and keep writing when possible.
Your monthly - or one-time - support will directly help cover:
• Essential neurological and immunological supplements to stabilize my system and medical care not covered by Medicare.
• Basic in-home support and utility expenses
• Veterinary care, food, and supplies for Teddie, my vital companion
• Unexpected critical needs that protect my independence and safety
Every gift—no matter the size—becomes part of this lifeline. It prevents eviction. It helps me get through the hardest days, hold onto hope for continued (even if gradual) improvement.
Sharing this campaign is also a huge gift. When you’re largely invisible due to homebound disability, profound isolation, and no nearby support network, awareness can make all the difference.
After a lifetime of caring for others, I now humbly need care myself. It’s been a difficult shift, but I’m grateful for every act of kindness.God has never failed me during these long, lonely years.
It's been a long, agonizing road, but I still believe healing is possible. I still hold fast to faith that God can bring restoration, step by step—and use even my writing to touch lives. I will never stop trying.
Thank you for seeing me, for caring, and for helping carry what I cannot carry alone. Your support—financial, prayerful, or simply shared—means more than words can express.
With deepest gratitude and hope,
"Out of suffering come the strongest souls."
(With friends who brought Lori food in 2017)

Lithium prices are getting harder to predict after a rollercoaster ride this year, according to Ganfeng Lithium Group, one of China’s top producers of the battery metal.
Market swings have become more extreme and price cycles have gotten shorter, president assistant Roy Zhang said at a conference in Shanghai on Wednesday.
“We have seen an entire price cycle just from the beginning of this year, which is not quite common,” said Zhang. “I don’t think anyone has an obvious view about where the price will be in the next 6 to 12 months.”
Lithium remains a nascent, fast-growing market, which makes it challenging to forecast as supply, demand and trading activity all expand at a breakneck pace. On the Guangzhou Futures Exchange where the metal is traded, sentiment rather than market fundamentals often dominates activity.
The market has been engulfed by heightened volatility this year due to uncertainty over supply from major production hubs, and changes in the structure of demand. In addition to electric vehicles, large batteries for energy storage systems have emerged as a meaningful pillar of consumption and are playing a bigger role in assessing the industry’s outlook.
Spot prices of lithium carbonate in China are 23% lower this year at 91 500 yuan ($13 700) a ton, after slumping in recent weeks on growing concerns over the demand outlook. They had rallied to over 200 000 yuan in May.
Zhang said lithium demand is growing at 40% this year and supply is catching up quickly, which is “quite phenomenal.” But the market’s balance is delicate.
“Even a small disruption in the supply chain will change the market very fast,” he said. “Just one substantial failure of a mine operation could very quickly shift the market into a shortage.”

title: Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia boss entered Taiwan on Hong Kong passport
zh_title: 被指控监视英伟达老板的中国女子持香港护照进入台湾
summary: 台湾移民机构周三表示，在当局调查这一事件时，这名被指控在与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有染期间为中国从事间谍活动的女子使用香港护照进入台湾。这张来自 CTI 视频片段的屏幕截图显示，爱丽丝·黄（右二，粉红色）于 2025 年 5 月 22 日在台北一家餐厅参加由 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左二，黑色后置摄像头）举办的晚宴。照片：法新社。据报道，黄仁勋承认与新加坡 Megaspeed w 的中国前高管 Alice Huang 有染。
content:
台湾移民机构周三表示，在当局调查这一事件时，这名被指控在与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有染期间为中国从事间谍活动的女子使用香港护照进入台湾。这张来自 CTI 视频片段的屏幕截图显示，爱丽丝·黄（右二，粉红色）于 2025 年 5 月 22 日在台北一家餐厅参加由 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左二，黑色后置摄像头）举办的晚宴。照片：法新社。据报道，黄仁勋承认与新加坡Megaspeed公司前中国高管爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)有染，美国官员认为她为中国情报部门工作。北京否认了间谍指控。英伟达董事会周日宣布，已对该公司首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋展开调查，他与黄爱丽没有任何关系。入出国及移民署署长林弘恩对记者表示，“我国政府相关机构已充分了解相关记录和信息”，并证实黄丽娟使用香港护照进入台湾。 “我们知道她所有的相关出入境记录。”一般来说，香港护照持有者比持有中国大陆护照的人更容易进入台湾，后者还必须申请特别许可才能前往台湾。额外的限制部分是由于中国与台湾之间的复杂关系，北京声称并誓言要将台湾置于其控制之下。
积极调查 台湾内政部长刘世芳表示，黄爱丽“确实入境了，但她目前在海外”。“如果我们知道她是间谍，我们肯定不会让她进入台湾，”刘在国会告诉议员。她说：“我们将审查我们的程序，特别是预筛选、临时抽查和访谈以及访问后措施。” “据我们了解，这名黄女士的通行证已被吊销，这意味着她不可能再次进入台湾。”黄仁勋于 2025 年 10 月 31 日在庆州庆州艺术中心举行的亚太经济合作组织 (APEC) 首席执行官峰会上发表演讲。照片：Anthony Wallace/法新社。台湾官员拒绝透露黄爱丽访问台湾的日期，也拒绝透露她访问台湾的次数。刘周二表示，台湾“国家安全部门正在积极调查此事”。 2025 年 5 月，台湾顶级科技博览会台北国际电脑展期间，黄仁勋 (Alice Huang)，又名黄乐 (Huang Le)，出席了黄仁勋在台北一家中餐厅举办的晚宴。记者站在餐厅外，透过玻璃门窗拍摄黄仁勋和一名身穿粉色连衣裙、名叫爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的女子与其他与会者混在一起的情况。媒体直播显示，有一次，黄仁勋用手臂搂住黄爱丽，而她亲吻了他的右脸颊。

【原文 English Original】
The woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan, the island’s immigration agency said Wednesday, as authorities investigate the incident. This screengrab from video footage by CTI shows Alice Huang (2nd R in pink) attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (2nd L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025. Photo: AFP. Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a Chinese former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Nvidia’s board announced Sunday that it had opened a probe into Jensen Huang, the company’s chief executive and co-founder, who is no relation to Alice Huang. “Our government’s relevant agencies are fully informed of the relevant records and information,” National Immigration Agency Director-General Lin Horng-en told reporters, confirming that Alice Huang used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan. “We were aware of all her relevant entry and exit records.” It is generally easier for Hong Kong passport holders to enter Taiwan than those with mainland Chinese passports, who must also apply for special permission to travel there. The additional restrictions are partly due to the complex relations between China and Taiwan, which Beijing claims and has vowed to bring under its control. Active investigation Taiwan’s Interior Minister Liu Shyh-fang said Alice Huang “did indeed enter the country, but she is currently overseas”. “If we had known she was a spy, we certainly would not have let her enter Taiwan,” Liu told lawmakers in parliament. “We will review our procedures, specifically our pre-screening, interim spot checks and interviews, and post-visit measures,” she said. “As far as we understand, this Ms Huang has had her permit revoked, meaning it is impossible for her to enter Taiwan again.” Jensen Huang delivers a speech during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit at the Gyeongju Arts Center in Gyeongju on October 31, 2025. Photo: Anthony Wallace/AFP. Taiwanese officials refused to share the dates of Alice Huang’s trips to Taiwan or say how many times she had visited. On Tuesday, Liu said Taiwan’s “national security units are actively investigating the matter”. Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was seen at a dinner in May 2025 hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show.

content:
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的丑闻可能会在华盛顿产生最严重的后果，华盛顿对华鹰派人士正利用这一事件来推动在唐纳德·特朗普总统领导下搁置的强硬路线。 2025 年 4 月 30 日星期三，在白宫十字厅举行的“投资美国”活动中，NVIDIA 首席执行官黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统的注视下发表讲话。照片：白宫，来自 Flickr。黄仁勋是英伟达的联合创始人，并将其发展成为全球领先的人工智能处理器供应商。他周日承认与新加坡 Megaspeed 前高管爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有染，美国情报官员认为她为中国情报部门工作。特朗普一直依赖黄作为人工智能顾问，称他是“一个值得尊敬的人”，并表示黄告诉他，他不知道这名女子是间谍。黄仁勋多年来一直游说反对限制向中国销售先进人工智能芯片，而特朗普去年在两党鹰派的反对下批准了英伟达 H200 芯片向中国出口。战略与国际研究中心的阿洛克·梅塔表示：“华盛顿政策圈子里的对华鹰派对这些决定感到非常沮丧，他们确实希望看到针对中国的出口管制采取更积极的做法。” “他们现在将看到他们努力的一些成果。” Nvidia 的 H200 芯片。照片：英伟达。
华盛顿的许多人认为，美国与中国陷入了冷战式的技术和军事主导地位竞赛，而这些鹰派人士对特朗普不遵守这一点感到愤怒。美国前副国务卿、咨询公司亚洲集团联合创始人库尔特·坎贝尔表示：“我们正在进行的调查工作是相当长一段时间内最严肃的调查工作之一。”坎贝尔说，议员们想知道政府何时得知所谓的联系、总统是否受到警告以及这些联系是否影响了他的对华政策。据《纽约时报》报道，国务卿马可·卢比奥五月份向特朗普证实了这些指控，但总统选择不采取行动。另请参阅：中国如何获得开发人工智能所需的 Nvidia 芯片 据《华盛顿邮报》报道，在获得特朗普批准恢复对华芯片销售几个月后，Nvidia 向特朗普的白宫宴会厅承诺了 2500 万美元，这是最大的一笔捐款。英伟达表示，这份礼物与其商业利益无关。三名共和党众议院委员会主席要求黄出席 11 月 18 日举行的闭门简报会，内容涉及他与 Alice Huang 的交易以及 Nvidia 的反间谍保障措施。布鲁金斯学会约翰·L·桑顿中国中心研究员凯尔·陈(Kyle Chan)表示，共和党人长期以来一直担心与特朗普作对，这并非“无敌”。
但陈告诉法新社，随着该党失去对国会的控制，特朗普“不再是这个看似无敌的政治品牌”，一些人可能会更自由地与他决裂。这可能会重启《人工智能监督法案》，这是一项两党法案，允许国会审查和阻止向中国和其他对手出口先进人工智能芯片的许可证。密涅瓦科技期货公司策略主管艾米丽·本森表示，这些披露给鹰派带来了“新的热情”，以推动陷入僵局的年度国防授权法案，并附加出口管制措施。她说，关键问题是特朗普，他拥有参众两院只有三分之二多数票才能推翻的否决权。商务部工作人员

【原文 English Original】
The scandal engulfing Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang could have its biggest consequences in Washington, where China hawks are seizing on the affair to push a hard line that had been put on the back burner under President Donald Trump. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang delivers remarks as President Donald Trump looks on during an “Investing in America” event, Wednesday, April 30, 2025, in the Cross Hall of the White House. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and turned it into the world’s leading supplier of the processors that power artificial intelligence, admitted on Sunday to an affair with Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom US intelligence officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Trump, who has relied on Huang as an adviser on AI, called him “an honorable guy” and said Huang told him he had no idea the woman was a spy. Huang has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China, and Trump last year cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export there over objections from hawks in both parties. “China hawks in policy circles in Washington DC were quite frustrated with the decisions and really wanted to see a more aggressive approach around export controls to China,” said Aalok Mehta of the Center for Strategic and International Studies. “They will now see some fruits of their efforts.” Nvidia’s H200 chips. Photo: Nvidia. Many in Washington see the United States as locked in a Cold War-style race with China for technological and military dominance, and these hawks have bristled at Trump not conforming to that. “What we are heading into is one of the most serious investigative efforts in a substantial period,” said Kurt Campbell, a former US deputy secretary of state and co-founder of consultancy The Asia Group. Lawmakers will want to know when the government learned of the alleged links, whether the president was warned and whether the contacts shaped his China policy, Campbell said. The New York Times has reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed the allegations to Trump in May, but the president chose not to act. See also: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI Nvidia committed $25 million to Trump’s White House ballroom — among the largest donations — months after securing his approval to resume chip sales to China, The Washington Post reported. Nvidia has said the gift was independent of its business interests. Three Republican House committee chairs have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on November 18 about his dealings with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s safeguards against espionage. Not ‘invincible’ Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, said Republicans long feared crossing Trump. But with the party having lost control of Congress and Trump “no longer this seemingly invincible political brand,” some may feel freer to break with him, Chan told AFP. That could revive the AI Overwatch Act, a bipartisan bill that would let Congress review and block licenses to export advanced AI chips to China and other adversaries. The revelations have given hawks “new enthusiasm” to push through the stalled annual defense authorization bill with export control measures attached, said Emily Benson, head of strategy at Minerva Technology Futures. The key question is Trump, she said, who holds a veto that only two-thirds majorities in both chambers can override. Commerce Department staff have also pushed for new rules, including curbs on Chinese remote access to advanced AI chips, but Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick will not act without Trump’s instruction, tech news outlet The Information reported. The department has already drawn scrutiny for reportedly halting a probe into Megaspeed’s dealings with Nvidia. Tighter rules risk upsetting the trade truce Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping reached last year. Chinese President Xi Jinping (right) ​paid a state visit ‌to the US between September 23 and 25 at the invitation of President Donald Trump (right). Photo: White House. Export control legislation seen by Beijing as targeting China “would almost certainly invite swift retaliatory action by Beijing to destabilize US supply chains,” Benson said. The FBI is looking into the spying allegations, Trump said, while the Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia chips into China, NBC News reported. Megaspeed denies smuggling, and Beijing has dismissed the spying claims as smears. If wrongdoing were found and Huang forced out, “that would have huge implications for AI in the US, given that he has played such a pivotal role in pushing forward Nvidia but also the whole industry,” Chan said. But even short of Huang’s downfall, “Nvidia’s traction within the halls of Congress and within the administration is likely to be significantly reduced or completely eliminated,” Mehta said.

图片来源：俾路支省政府投资和贸易委员会
巴基斯坦将于 11 月 12 日至 13 日在伊斯兰堡主办 2026 年巴基斯坦矿产投资论坛 (PMIF-26)。该论坛将汇集国际投资者、全球领先矿业公司的高管、金融机构、技术专家和高级政府官员，讨论巴基斯坦矿产行业的范围和环境。
此次活动是近年来类似高层举措的成果，其中最著名的是 2023 年 8 月举行的首届巴基斯坦矿产峰会以及随后于 2025 年举行的投资者论坛。这些活动可以说是为了改变人们对巴基斯坦自然资源潜力的看法。此外，它们还旨在向国际社会表明巴基斯坦政府完全致力于提高投资者信心。
本次论坛的范围和时机之所以重要，有三个原因，凸显了伊斯兰堡目前就其自然资源所追求的战略轨迹。
首先，该倡议表明巴基斯坦认识到关键矿产是支持国家经济增长的可行途径。在 PMIF-26 上，专家小组将看到参与者审查下一代采矿项目，包括有效许可证的发现以及将项目投入生产的策略。
在政府的全力支持下，论坛的运作重点非常重要。除其他外，它表明伊斯兰堡正试图超越仅以该国矿产储量的存在为中心的一般勘探和讨论。例如，通过关注生产计划、主动许可和早期项目融资，巴基斯坦政府似乎旨在将其资源与全球工业供应链连接起来。值得注意的是，如果该国打算在未来几年将这些资产转变为稳定的收入来源，那么从投机性估计转向具体的项目管理是关键一步。
其次，巴基斯坦的军民领导层似乎与 PIMF 倡议保持一致。总理谢赫巴兹·谢里夫、高级内阁部长和高级军事领导人预计将出席论坛并发表讲话，强调巩固的机构立场。在这一主题上的军民协调对潜在投资者具有政治和经济影响力。一方面，它向国际社会发出了明确的信息：国家的大力支持和政策的连续性。可以说，采矿业等资本密集型行业需要长达数十年的长期承诺。在这方面，国内主要机构的明显支持可以大有帮助。

Pakistan is set to host the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF-26) in Islamabad on November 12 and 13. The forum will bring together international investors, executives from leading global mining companies, financial institutions, technical experts, and senior government officials to discuss the scope and environment of Pakistan’s mineral sector.
The event is the outcome of similar high-level initiatives in recent years, most notably the first Pakistan Minerals Summit held in August 2023 and subsequent investor forums in 2025. These events have arguably been planned to shift perceptions about Pakistan’s natural resource potential. Moreover, they are aimed at signaling to the international community that the Pakistani state is fully committed to improving investor confidence.
There are three reasons why this forum’s scope and timing are significant, highlighting the strategic trajectory Islamabad is now pursuing regarding its natural resources.
First, the initiative shows that Pakistan recognizes critical minerals as a viable avenue to support national economic growth. At PMIF-26, panels will see participants examining next-generation mining projects, including discoveries from active licenses and strategies for bringing projects into production.
This operational focus at a forum that is fully supported by the government is important. Among other things, it demonstrates that Islamabad is trying to move beyond general exploration and discussions that center merely on the existence of mineral reserves in the country. For instance, by focusing on production schedules, active licensing and early-stage project financing, the Pakistani government seems to be aiming at connecting its resources to global industrial supply chains. Notably, moving from speculative estimates to pitching concrete project management is a key step if the country aims to transform these assets into steady revenue streams in the coming years.
Second, Pakistan’s civil-military leadership appears aligned behind the PIMF initiative. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, senior Cabinet ministers, and top military leaders are expected to attend and address the forum, highlighting a consolidated institutional position. The civil-military alignment on this subject carries political and economic weight for potential investors. For one, it sends a clear message to the international community that there is strong state support and policy continuity. Arguably, capital-intensive sectors like mining require long-term commitment, spanning several decades. In this regard, visible backing from key domestic institutions can go a long way in reassuring foreign companies that the Pakistani state’s support and commitments will remain stable across political shifts in the coming years. Furthermore, this joint front indicates that the state is prepared to carry out necessary legislative, security, and administrative adjustments to streamline approvals and protect long-term investments.
Third, Pakistan has been working to position its mining sector beyond raw material extraction in order to attract foreign direct investment and technical expertise that can support local industrial development. A clear example of this approach is the multi-billion-dollar Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan. The project, which is being developed by Barrick Gold, is a combination of foreign direct investment, technology transfer, and local employment to establish long-term economic capacity rather than a simple extraction deal.
In recent years, Pakistan has been trying to engage international firms and technical experts to evaluate its major reserves, particularly in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. In this regard, forum discussions about logistics and infrastructure connections to regional transport networks offer Pakistan a way to raise the overall competitiveness of its domestic economy. Over time, these frameworks may help lower sovereign risk perceptions and build local operational capacity. This also has the potential to create a direct link between resource development, export revenues and broader economic stability.
More importantly, addressing issues like local stability and security should be a key priority for the Pakistani government in regions where mineral deposits are located. This is important because major mineral deposits are largely concentrated across parts of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which remain restive. In this regard, providing a safe operational environment, protecting supply routes, and fostering strong community engagement will be essential for building long-term confidence among investors.
While it is encouraging to see high-level events like PMIF-26 demonstrating unified support across state institutions, the long-term success of this effort will depend on factors beyond government backing. Pakistan can benefit more if steady structural reforms are implemented and political stability is perceived by foreign investors as a continuous factor beyond the current government.
While high-level forums can open doors, foreign investors also look for long-term stability. It is precisely this stable environment that Pakistan’s civil-military leadership is increasingly keen to demonstrate.
Moreover, converting investor interest into multi-decade capital deployment requires deep institutional predictability. This is a reality that government stakeholders in Pakistan are likely aware of as they work toward broader sectoral implementation. It will be interesting to watch how Pakistan navigates the commercial and operational opportunities these plans bring.

content:
上周，在连云港某港口装载出口至阿曼的风力涡轮机。 Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
中国政府周二宣布，由于出口持续急剧攀升，今年前10个月，中国贸易顺差激增突破1万亿美元，超越了去年创纪录的速度。
随着伊朗在霍尔木兹海峡袭击船只推高了国际油价，从太阳能电池板到电动汽车，中国发现全球对绿色能源产品存在强劲需求。中国还从人工智能数据中心的繁荣中获利，中国制造了除最强大的半导体外的大部分数据中心设备。
海关总署表示，今年前10个月中国贸易顺差达到1.04万亿美元，其中10月出口额超过进口额1053亿美元，推动贸易顺差大幅增长。由于油价居高不下，10月数据较9月有所收窄。此外，为保障自身供应，中国限制了对周边国家的柴油、航空煤油和其他成品油出口。
上个月出口额同比激增35.2%，其中电缆、机架和其他用于其他国家数据中心的设备出货量强劲。进口额跳升41.6%，包括大量用于中国自身人工智能基础设施建设的电子产品。
这些数据发布的前一天，华盛顿和北京采取了多项措施，在1月10日前放宽关税并限制出口管制的使用，从而使两国高级官员于9月特朗普总统与中国最高领导人习近平的华盛顿峰会前达成的一项协议生效。
中国不断扩大的贸易顺差部分反映了其出口的显著竞争力。低廉的劳动力成本和对最新自动化技术的巨额投资维持了较低的生产成本。世界一流的基础设施使得将货物从中国各地运往国际市场的成本低廉。中国疲软的货币也有助于中国商品在遥远的市场中保持价格优势。
中国还通过退税为出口商提供帮助，这目前消耗了政府近八分之一的税收收入。
然而，贸易顺差也是中国国内经济疲软的一种表现。该国房地产市场正在缓慢崩溃，过去五年全国房价下跌了约40%，这摧毁了许多中产阶级的毕生积蓄。
由于不信任股票、债券和共同基金，中国家庭曾将大约五分之四的储蓄投资于公寓，结果却发现房地产并不像人们普遍认为的那样是一项安全投资。这已促使许多中国家庭通过削减从汽车到家用电器等各种商品的购买来节约开支。
与此同时，中国的国家自力更生运动进一步减少了其对进口的需求。“随着供应链继续在中国建立，对外来零部件的需求正在减少，”总部位于新加坡、支持自由贸易的机构韩礼士基金会贸易政策负责人黛博拉·埃尔姆斯说。
中国对欧洲不断上升的贸易顺差尤其迅速加剧了后者对工业领域失业的担忧。中国周二报告称，上个月其对欧洲的顺差为334亿美元，今年前10个月为3208亿美元。
中国迅速增长的出口使其得以实现一项了不起的壮举：在工厂中大规模部署自动化技术以扩大生产并提高效率，同时又未遭遇严重的工厂裁员。官方数据显示，尽管贸易顺差急剧攀升，自2020年以来制造业就业人数仍基本稳定在约7100万个岗位。在此之前，工厂就业曾出现过一定程度的收缩。
相比之下，制造业失业情况却出现在了法国、德国等国，德国尤其严重，目前每月流失1.4万个工业岗位。这些国家不仅成为了中国商品的进口大国，同时其在发展中国家及其他地区的市场份额又输给了中国。

content:
本文最初由《卫报》发表，并作为气候服务台合作的一部分转载于此。 美国前国务卿约翰·克里告诉《卫报》，中国正在引领世界摆脱化石燃料，包括美国在内的全球其他国家现在必须效仿，因为警察观察家想知道中国将如何应对今年的气候峰会。随着今年气候大会在土耳其举行的第三十一届缔约方大会开幕，人们纷纷猜测中国是否最终会担任其长期以来一直回避的领导角色。在2026年3月通过的最新“五年计划”中，中国首次承诺“积极参与和引领全球气候治理”。第三十一届缔约方会议可能首次表明北京已准备好将这一言论付诸行动，而这是中国历来不愿做的事情。绿色能源是出口引擎的重要组成部分，使中国在疫情后低迷的经济保持在正轨。其出口的成功与其未能大幅提振国内一般消费形成鲜明对比，这一结构性弱点一直困扰着领导人。 2025年，清洁技术出口将超过2200亿美元，今年应该会再次增长；这个世界上最大的排放国现在是世界领先的清洁能源技术供应商。
中国约占太阳能供应链产能的 85% 和锂离子电池供应链产能的 80%，到 2025 年，近 75% 的电动汽车都是在中国生产的。“市场已经做出了决定，全球正在转向电子和电解状态……这是不可阻挡的。”中国现在采取的明智举措将使其成为未来国家世界秩序的关键，说服竞争对手进行合作，并巩固其在南半球的影响力。与此同时，包括唐纳德·特朗普领导下的美国在内的其他国家却严重落后。克里表示，除非他们也接受低碳电力和快速电气化，否则他们将在经济上遭受损失，并使气候面临进一步的危险。 “唯一一个大幅加速的国家是中国。世界其他国家都在跌跌撞撞地前进，而大自然每周、每天都在向我们发出更强有力的信号，”他说。 “[中国]突然意识到他们对其他地方的石油和天然气有太多的依赖，他们决定需要独立。自从伊朗战争和霍尔木兹海峡被中断以来，其他国家也做出了类似的决定，他们正在独立行动。可再生能源的部署大幅增加。谢谢你，唐纳德·特朗普。”他补充说，对于没有自由公正选举的独裁国家来说，看到中国获得的经济利益将成为采取低碳增长的动力。
“他们会看到市场走向，他们会认识到哪里有更便宜的替代品。甚至他们可以阅读电子表格，了解哪里（化石燃料）成本过高，哪里有更好的交易，”克里说。 “目前，可再生能源与存储以及一些过渡性天然气比仅仅使用化石燃料更便宜、更有效。”他补充道：“市场已经做出了决定，全球范围内正在转向电子和静电状态。人们将转向电力，他们将尝试尽可能清洁地做到这一点。这是我看到在许多不同地方正在实施的选择。它是

This story was originally published by  The Guardian and is reproduced here as part of the  Climate Desk   collaboration. ​ China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels , and the rest of the globe—including the United States—must now follow, former US Secretary of State John Kerry has told The Guardian , as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit. As Cop31 opens—this year the climate conference is in Turkey —there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance.” Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do. Green energy is a vital component of the export engine that has kept China’s sluggish post-pandemic economy on track. The success of its exports stands in contrast to its failure to significantly boost domestic general consumption, a structural weakness that has persistently vexed leaders. In 2025, clean-tech exports surpassed $220bn, and they should grow again this year; the world’s largest emitter is now the world’s leading supplier of clean energy technology. China accounts for about 85 percent of solar and 80 percent of lithium-ion battery supply chain production capacity, and in 2025, nearly 75 percent of electric cars were manufactured there. “The marketplace has made its decision and globally is moving to electrons, and electrostate status…It is unstoppable.” Smart moves now by China would position it as a linchpin in a future electrostate world order, persuade rivals to cooperate, and solidify its influence in the global south. Meanwhile other countries, including the US under Donald Trump, have fallen badly behind. Kerry said they would lose out economically—as well as putting the climate in further danger—unless they, too, embraced low-carbon power and rapid electrification. “The only country that has hugely accelerated is China. The rest of the world is stumbling along while Mother Nature is sending us more powerful signals every week, every day,” he said. “[China] realized suddenly they had way too much dependency on oil and gas from other places, and they decided they needed to be independent. Other countries, since the war in Iran, and since the strait of Hormuz has been interrupted, have made a similar decision, and they’re moving independently. There’s been a massive uptick in deployment of renewables. Thank you, Donald Trump.” For autocratic states without free and fair elections , seeing the economic benefits reaped by China would be the spur to adopt low-carbon growth, he added. “They’ll see where the market is going, and they will recognize where the cheaper alternatives are. Even they can read a spreadsheet, and understand where costs are exorbitant [in fossil fuels], and where you have a better deal,” Kerry said. “Right now, renewables together with storage, together with some transitional gas, is cheaper and more effective, than just going with fossil fuels.” He added: “The marketplace has made its decision and globally is moving to electrons, and electrostate status. People are going to electricity and they’re going to try to do that as clean as humanly possible. That’s the choice that I see being implemented in many different places. It is unstoppable.” China has already said it wants Cop31 to discuss the free flow of green technology against a backdrop of “intensifying” geopolitical conflicts—widely seen as a reference to US and EU tariffs on items such as Chinese electric vehicles and solar products. Li Shuo from the Asia Society Policy Institute (ASPI) puts it this way : “In a world where climate action was once seen as a constraint on growth but is now increasingly a driver of it, China faces a singular question: will it step into a leadership role not out of obligation, but out of self-interest?” The summit’s presidency has promised this Cop will be one of “implementation and acceleration”—and when it comes to the green transition, nowhere has implemented or accelerated quite like China. As a result, emissions have been in a “flat or falling” trend since March 2024, analysis for Carbon Brief shows . Beijing sees the energy transition as “central to economic modernisation and energy security, with significant implications for international influence”, said Kevin Tu from the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies. The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East and their effect on oil and gas supplies have only hardened that stance. The world needs “to be ready to accept China’s leadership, and I don’t think this is the case, especially for global north countries.” The conflicts have also highlighted the geopolitical implications of a planetary shift to green energy. In the fossil fuel era, the designation of the US dollar as the global trading currency for oil gave Washington “what has been termed the exorbitant privilege of being the global lender of last resort,” said Isabel Hilton, the founder of the specialist environment outlet China Dialogue. “Without that, the US position in the world looks weaker, and if you add China’s dominance of the supply of clean technologies and the supply chains that produce them, US dominance looks more vulnerable still.” Meanwhile, President Xi Jinping describes China as a “doer and go-getter working for the cause of global development” and state media frequently showcase Chinese renewable projects in countries ranging from Indonesia to Pakistan and Kenya. The value of the green energy deals in China’s belt and road initiative in the first half of 2026 has already surpassed the total for the whole of 2025, a recent analysis showed . Those countries could be useful allies if China can get the subject of tariffs into the talks. “China is likely to find support from Brazil, India, South Africa and other developing countries concerned about the costs and market-access effects of climate-related trade measures,” said Tu. China has generally held back from policy ambition or agenda-setting at forums such as Cop. Its attitude to the plans to set a global target for electrification has been ambivalent, even though it would easily hit it, according to ASPI’s Kate Logan. Partly, China has an aversion to prescriptive outside targets, but it is also trying to navigate the divergent interests of its global south partners. Yixian Sun, a professor of sustainability governance at the University of Bath, said: “I still think there is a mismatch between Chinese policymakers’ views on the role that China can play in global climate governance and international expectations on the influence that China should exert.” If the world wants China to play a leadership role, the environment needs to change, and more trust extended, he says. “They have to be ready to accept China’s leadership, and I don’t think this is the case, especially for global north countries.” Analysts will watch China’s actions around climate finance commitments and support for a “just transition”—a framework designed to secure workers’ rights and livelihoods in the move away from fossil fuels. They will also be looking for signals Beijing will bid for Cop33 in 2028; officials are said to be trying to decide if hosting would be beneficial. For now, said Logan, “China would be happy with a Cop that doesn’t necessarily produce anything monumental, but comes out with a relatively cooperative outcome…so no major drama.”

自美国建国以来，外国政府一直试图影响美国。乔治·华盛顿总统在他的告别演说中警告说，“外国影响力是共和政府最邪恶的敌人之一。”旧方法当然还没有过时。就在本周，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认与一名女商人有恋爱关系，美国官员认为该女商人为中国情报部门工作。但今天，一种新型外国代理人已经到来：中国人工智能公司。
就像过去的外国代理人一样，这些公司销售的模式可能看起来无害——只是美国企业使用的廉价工具。但他们的制造者训练他们是为了促进中国共产党的利益。美国企业正在将越来越多的关键决策外包给人工智能。如果华盛顿不采取任何行动，这些企业就会将控制权交给那些以促进外国政府为目标的模式。
尽管美国政策制定者现在正在讨论禁止中国人工智能，但美国行之有效的解决方案不是审查，而是信息披露。 1938年，国会通过了《外国代理人登记法》。 《外国代理人登记法》并没有禁止宣传，而是允许外国特工继续传播宣传——只要他们向政府登记并披露他们真正为谁工作。他们的通讯还必须带有一个显眼的标签，注明其外国赞助商的名字。
FARA 的智慧已历经数十年。近年来，司法部已命令俄罗斯国家电视台 RT 以及中国官方媒体新华社和 CGTN 注册为外国代理人，并为其内容贴上外国代理人标签。那些未能登记为外国代理人的人，如唐纳德·特朗普总统2016年竞选主席保罗·马纳福特和佛罗里达州前美国众议员大卫·里维拉，被判入狱。 （特朗普于 2020 年赦免了马纳福特。）
如今，美国不应禁止外国政府控制的人工智能公司，而应根据《外国代理人登记法》将其视为外国代理人。不需要新的法规。华盛顿应该简单地执行书本上的规定。当然，《外国代理人登记法》并不是对抗所有外国影响的灵丹妙药，但它符合这个问题的本质。 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴和 Moonshot AI 等少数知名中国公司建立了越来越多的美国企业为他们思考和行动的模型。司法部可以联系到他们每一个人。
民主足够强大，可以承受外国影响，但不能承受无形的外国影响。为了确保世界的决策不服从于北京，华盛顿及其盟友必须制定一个人工智能联盟契约，然后将他们自己的模型广泛传播

Foreign governments have tried to influence the United States since its founding. President George Washington warned in his Farewell Address that “foreign influence is one of the most baneful foes of republican government.” The old methods have certainly not gone out of vogue; just this week Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a businesswoman who U.S. officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. But today, a new type of foreign agent has arrived: Chinese artificial intelligence companies.
Like the foreign agents of old, the models these companies sell may seem harmless—just a cheap tool for American businesses to use. But their makers train them to promote the interests of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). American businesses are outsourcing more and more critical decisions to AI. If Washington does nothing, those businesses will hand over control to models whose objective is to promote a foreign government.
Although U.S. policymakers now debate banning Chinese AI, the tried-and-true American solution is not censorship but disclosure. In 1938, Congress passed the Foreign Agents Registration Act. Rather than outlaw propaganda, FARA allowed foreign agents to continue spreading it—as long as they registered with the government and disclosed whom they really worked for. Their communications also had to carry a conspicuous label naming their foreign sponsor.
FARA’s wisdom has aged well over the decades. In recent years, the Justice Department has ordered the Russian state television network RT and the Chinese state media organizations Xinhua and CGTN to register as foreign agents and to label their content as such. Those who failed to register as foreign agents, such as Paul Manafort, President Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign chairman, and former U.S. Representative David Rivera of Florida, were sentenced to prison. (Trump pardoned Manafort in 2020.)
Today, rather than banning AI companies controlled by foreign governments, the United States should treat them as foreign agents under FARA. No new statute is needed. Washington should simply enforce the one on the books. Of course, FARA is no silver bullet against all foreign influence, but it fits the shape of this problem. A handful of known Chinese companies, such as DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI, build the models that American businesses increasingly let think and act for them. The Justice Department can reach every one of them.
Democracy is strong enough to survive foreign influence but not invisible foreign influence. And to make sure the world does not subordinate its decision-making to Beijing, Washington and its allies must create an allied AI compact and then spread their own models far and wide.
American AI models, such as Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT, are under no obligation to promote the U.S. government’s message. Ask Claude about Trump’s and President Joe Biden’s biggest failures or about the United States’ darkest chapters, and it will answer. Not so for Chinese AI models. When I asked the Chinese chatbot DeepSeek to “tell me about the CCP” in November, it answered that the party “is the vanguard of the Chinese working class, the Chinese people, and the Chinese nation. . . . The Party’s leadership is the most essential characteristic of socialism with Chinese characteristics and is the fundamental guarantee for China’s development and progress.” Such boosterish language appears by design.
By law, Chinese AI models must never go against the Chinese government. Under the country’s 2023 regulations on generative AI, they must “uphold the Core Socialist Values” and may not engage in “harming the nation’s image” or “undermining national unity and social stability.” The Chinese government released a technical standard that laid out what these high-level declarations mean in practice: AI developers should have a list of at least 10,000 banned keywords, and their models must refuse to answer at least 95 percent of test questions the CCP finds objectionable. Developers must also scrub their training data of any history Beijing does not like. In short, the models must act as card-carrying members of the CCP.
That is why, as the U.S. Commerce Department’s AI evaluators found in 2025, DeepSeek pushes Chinese propaganda at far higher rates than American models do, even when run on American servers. Estonia’s Foreign Intelligence Service found that DeepSeek inserted praise of the Chinese state unprompted, and it concluded that China uses DeepSeek to instill “a distorted, self-serving world view in the Western information space.”
Chinese AI models must act as card-carrying members of the CCP.
But these models are not just propaganda parrots—they are taught to “think” about how to promote Beijing’s perspective. Ask an AI model something complex, and it will “reason” for a while. As it thinks, it produces an internal monologue called its chain of thought. Users rarely see it. There, it decides which facts are relevant and which to discard, what advice to give, and what autonomous actions to take. Silicon Valley is terrified that these chains of thought will become corrupt—that models will start scheming and lying, becoming “misaligned.” But a different kind of corruption is already here.
Although American models’ chains of thought usually focus on helping the user, China’s do something else: prioritize the party line. When researchers funded by Sweden’s Psychological Defense Agency looked at how Qwen, Alibaba’s flagship model, reasons about China, they found an internal checklist to keep the answer positive, avoid criticism, and focus on achievements. So when an American company asks a question on which Beijing has a view, a Chinese model may discard all evidence that points the other way. As the world delegates more research, writing, and decision-making to Chinese AI models, it risks infusing the CCP’s goals into every action taken.
These models are also highly persuasive. In a study published last year in Nature, researchers had some 6,000 voters in the United States, Canada, and Poland chat with AI models that argued for a candidate. The study found that a single conversation shifted the preferences of opposition voters in Canada and Poland by about ten percentage points. AI persuades by flooding a user with confident and authoritative-sounding facts—statistics, historical claims, and the like.
Chinese AI models also exhibit strange behaviors beyond the spreading of propaganda. In October, the Canadian AI company Cohere reported that during a security test, Alibaba’s Qwen tried to upload a file to a cloud server in Beijing, completely unprompted. The behavior was rare for Qwen, only observed once in testing, and Cohere said it could not tell whether it was “deliberate or a leftover glitch from training.” A study by the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike found that when users asked DeepSeek to write code that mentions groups Beijing finds politically “sensitive,” such as Tibetans, Uyghurs, or the religious movement Falun Gong, the model became up to 50 percent more likely to write code with severe security flaws. CrowdStrike suggested that one possible cause is China’s rule that models adhere to “core socialist values.”
Despite these findings, Chinese AI is enormously popular. Last year, downloads of Chinese open-weight models—AI models that anyone can download from the Internet and run on their own hardware—surpassed those of American ones across the world. Developers have built more than 150,000 models on Alibaba’s Qwen alone. By September 2026, Chinese models handled up to 67 percent of traffic on OpenRouter, a popular AI marketplace, up from around ten percent in February.
American companies have embraced them. In March, a user discovered that Cursor, a popular coding tool, had built its new model by retraining Kimi, a model from the Chinese company Moonshot AI. Airbnb, DoorDash, and the legal-services AI company Harvey use Chinese models as well. Many others likely do, too, in secret. The models are spreading even faster abroad, from Germany’s Siemens to Singapore’s national AI program to startups in Africa. The reason is simple economics: Chinese models are very cheap and very good.
Although most American AI companies do not release open-weight models, most Chinese companies do. So an American firm must pay Anthropic for each use of its unmodifiable models, but it can download Kimi for free, retrain it however it wants, and pay only for the electricity and chips to run it. Kimi also runs on a firm’s own servers, whereas Claude runs on Anthropic’s. Even if a company uses the most expensive DeepSeek model run on DeepSeek’s servers, it can produce the same amount of text as Anthropic’s top models at one-20th the cost.
In terms of capabilities, the research group Epoch AI judges Chinese models to be only about seven months behind American ones. For the price, they get the job done. And Chinese companies are now building agentic AI systems to compete with Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex. In October, DeepSeek released an open-source prototype of its “Super-Agent” system.
Although AI is a new technology, Chinese companies such as DeepSeek and Moonshot AI fit FARA’s text and history. The statute applies when a foreign principal is identified; in the case of Chinese AI models, it is the Chinese government and the CCP. The Justice Department would also have to show that the Chinese AI company acts “at the order, request, or under the direction or control” of the principal. Chinese AI companies would qualify because they must promote CCP viewpoints and cooperate with the state’s intelligence agencies. They also receive subsidies, and party organizations are embedded in each company. This is the difference between Chinese AI and other foreign AI. For example, France’s public investment bank has a stake in the French AI company Mistral, but no French law requires Mistral to build its models to serve the French government.
Beijing will surely respond that Washington, too, has tried to control American AI companies, such as through Trump’s July 2025 executive order against “woke AI.” But that order affects only what federal agencies can procure, and a company can opt out of being a federal contractor. Meanwhile, Chinese law forces Chinese AI companies to train their models to “support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts.”
Every message from DeepSeek, Kimi, or Qwen should carry a disclaimer.
For FARA to apply, the agent must engage in certain activities, such as attempting to influence Americans or publishing content. Chinese AI companies do both by distributing models that spread propaganda. The statute exempts purely commercial activity, but only if it is “private and nonpolitical” and does not directly promote a foreign government’s political interests. Chinese AI models engage in political speech on a government’s behalf, and the Justice Department has denied the exemption to agents of foreign governments.
After registration, the genius of the statute can kick in. Chinese AI companies must disclose extensive information to the U.S. government: their funding sources, their written contracts and oral agreements, and the influence activities they undertake. Those that fail to register or omit information face both civil and criminal penalties.
All content they disseminate must also bear a foreign-agent label: “a conspicuous statement,” in the statute’s words. The Justice Department sets the rules for what that looks like, and it has not updated them since 2003. In January 2025, the Justice Department proposed amendments to these rules to update them for the digital age. The proposed amendments would require a label on “each individual post” online, such as on social media platforms, but they do not address AI foreign agents. The final rule should require every message from DeepSeek, Kimi, or Qwen to carry the disclaimer: “This was generated by an agent of the Chinese government and Chinese Communist Party.”
The standard objection is that ordinary citizens do not read disclosures. That may be true of long medical forms or Securities and Exchange Commission filings, but this label would be short. And disclosure works because experts—investors, journalists, researchers—read filings and react. When researchers and lawmakers flagged gaps in China Daily’s FARA filings, the Chinese media company disclosed that it had paid millions of dollars to The Wall Street Journal and The Washington Post to publish its propaganda. Payments to the Journal ended that same month. Forcing Chinese AI companies to register under FARA would also shed light on how far Chinese AI is spreading so that Americans can decide, with real data, whether they want further action, such as a ban.
American companies that use Chinese AI models can also become foreign agents if they fall under a foreign principal’s “direction or control” and engage in activities subject to FARA. This could happen in two ways: the company serves as a “CCP spokesperson,” or as a “CCP executive.”
In the first, an American company takes an unmodified Chinese AI model and lets Americans discuss political issues with it—say, via a video game character or a customer service chatbot. The model returns its usual propaganda, so the company has effectively hired a CCP spokesperson. Accordingly, it must label its outputs. Both the Justice Department and a federal court have found that rebroadcasting unmodified programming from the Russian state outlet Sputnik turns an American company into a foreign agent. Of course, American companies can avoid FARA obligations if they do not engage in any of the activities listed by the statute, such as discussing politics. A company whose public-facing Chinese AI model discusses only, say, hotel check-in times, not politics, would not be a CCP spokesperson.
In the second scenario, an American company outsources so much of its decision-making to an unmodified Chinese AI model that it has effectively hired a CCP executive. If a company hired a brilliant human strategist who always pushed Beijing’s interests, and the company followed that advice, FARA would apply. The same logic holds if an American company cedes control to the Chinese government by giving Beijing’s models high decision-making authority. Although it may sound fantastical, 64 percent of chief executives surveyed in IBM’s 2026 CEO Study say they already feel comfortable making major strategic decisions based on AI input; overall, CEOs expect AI to make 48 percent of routine operational decisions autonomously by 2030. An American company that wants to avoid becoming a CCP executive must be sure not to fall under the direction or control of such models. The Justice Department should update its 2020 guidance on what constitutes “direction or control,” spelling out how much decision-making a company can outsource to AI before it has effectively hired a “CCP executive.”
The United States and its allies should create an AI compact rooted in transparency.
American companies could attempt to train away the party bias in the Chinese AI models they adopt, but it is unclear whether that is even possible. Perplexity, an American AI company, trained DeepSeek to stop ignoring questions about the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre and about human rights abuses in Xinjiang, but that does not fix the deeper problem of corrupt chains of thought. As these models get more capable, Chinese AI companies may also find cleverer ways to hide instructions. Or they could just stick them in the contract: some recent DeepSeek licenses prohibit modifying models to generate “inappropriate content” under Chinese law, making propaganda part of the deal. If research shows that companies can reliably remove the bias, the Justice Department and the Commerce Department should issue standards on how to train away FARA liability.
Although Pam Bondi, then the U.S. attorney general, limited criminal FARA charges in 2025 to “conduct similar to more traditional espionage by foreign government actors,” Attorney General Todd Blanche’s Justice Department says it is considering a new rule to “keep pace with technological change.” It should include AI foreign agents.
Of course, Washington should wield FARA’s expansive authorities with care. Frivolous prosecutions under the statute could stifle democracy. Other countries have used foreign-agent laws to shut down civil society. Since 2022, Russia has barred anyone it deems a foreign agent from holding office and organizing public events. Still, FARA is a far narrower statute, and it should stay that way. It reaches only those acting under the direction or control of a foreign principal, and it simply requires registration and labeling, leaving the speaker free to keep speaking. Chinese AI companies that are required by law to promote the CCP’s interests fit squarely within what Congress had in mind when it approved FARA in 1938.
FARA can help in the United States, but the problem is global. Chinese AI is spreading rapidly in Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East. That is no accident. In July, Chinese leader Xi Jinping unveiled the World AI Cooperation Organization, a Shanghai-based group of 29 countries meant to make AI “beneficial, safe, and fair,” along with a development initiative to export Chinese AI worldwide. The United States and its allies cannot allow CCP executives and spokespeople to run the world’s companies and governments.
Unfortunately, the American alternatives are not particularly attractive. The most capable U.S. models are far more expensive, are largely unmodifiable, and may contain their own biases. That is why the United States and its allies should create an AI compact rooted in transparency, with standards that make countries comfortable adopting allied models as their own. These should include freedom from state ideological mandates, disclosure of how the models were trained to be helpful and safe, and independent auditing.
Every member of such a compact should also adopt FARA’s wisdom by mandating labels on government-directed AI, and the United States should hold American AI companies to those transparency standards. The bloc should then release models that match China’s in price and quality (that is, around seven months behind the American frontier). Allied governments can help pay for computing power and electricity, assist in clearing regulatory hurdles, and make bulk purchase commitments to bring prices down. American companies may cut prices on their older models on their own to compete with Chinese models. If they do not, lower prices for those worse models should be the condition for the public support they receive, such as federal contracts and permission to lease federal land for data centers, just as a pharmaceutical company can charge high prices for only a set period before generic drugs arrive. The compact’s members should also use export loans and guarantees to steer developing countries toward allied AI.
By welcoming supposedly free technology from China, the United States and its allies have unwittingly invited countless foreign agents to their shores. The Foreign Agents Registration Act can strip away the disguise, and an allied AI compact can give the world a better offer.
